Every suppressive action these vengeful partisans take shows their true colors. For all their talk about election integrity, voter ID, and not harming eligible voters, closing legitimate polling places to make it harder to vote only has one logical end result.
Attacks by opponents of voting rights on young voters, mail-in ballots, early voting, and more aren't about integrity and fairness. It's about protecting their own power at any cost and tilting the playing field before the game has even been played.
We must stand up to stop them at every turn. RUSH $35 or more today to help us fight back in North Carolina and beyond >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=062726_5&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
NC Newsline: Amid protests, NC elections board rejects campus voting sites and Sunday voting in several counties [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=062726_5&amount=25]
We're now facing the repercussions of the partisan election takeover laws that went into effect at the end of 2024, Team.
To refresh your memory: After the 2024 elections and the defeat of a MAGA candidate for governor, opponents of voting rights in North Carolina jammed through a bill that took the power of the governor to appoint people to election boards and handed that to the state auditor . It's worth noting that the state auditor is the only statewide elected Republican, with Democrats winning the 2024 races for governor, lieutenant governor, attorney general, and secretary of state.
Now, among massive protests from young voters, the MAGA-fied North Carolina State Elections Board recently shot down proposals to continue having early voting sites on several universities around the state . These weren't new sites either; these were places where North Carolina had provided early voting locations for a decade or more.
This is voter suppression, plain and simple, by making it harder for eligible, registered voters to vote in-person by taking away their polling place. It's another demonstration of how opponents of voting rights in North Carolina are more focused on expanding and cementing their own power than they are in serving the people and having fair elections.
We have to fight these suppressive actions in North Carolina and any other state where opponents of voting rights try to replicate this. Step up with $35 or whatever you can today to help every eligible voter cast their ballot >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=062726_5&amount=35]

These new, highly partisan State Election Board members wouldn't even look the protestors in the eye or engage with their proposals. After the vote, Chairman Francis De Luca threatened to call the cops on students if they didn’t leave.
Need to better understand how this impacts young voters? Western Carolina University in Jackson County, for example, has had a polling place on campus since 2016 that’s been used in five general elections and four primaries, according to a document prepared for the board. The state board voted 3-2 to get rid of it.
Closing the campus voting site would not save money, but “ would create barriers to voting for young, rural residents ,” Jackson County Board member Betsy Swift told the state board. 64% of students don’t have vehicles to drive to the polling place, she said.
Without the on-campus site, the closest polling place for students will be a recreation center nearly two miles away. Students without transportation will have to walk along a four-lane highway and through a meadow to get there.
Voter suppression isn't just black and white photos of eligible voters being turned away from polling places. Voter suppression is making it harder for eligible voters to take part in our elections through onerous ID requirements, closing polling places, taking away voting locations, or ending mail-in voting. Every time someone makes it harder to cast your ballot, voters are suppressed.
It's not going to end until we stop them.

On Friday morning over 600 hundred Louisianans showed up to the Louisiana state capitol to protest and speak out against a new Congressional map proposed by the Louisiana GOP that will erase Louisiana's two black majority districts and establish all white districts.
During the hearing on redistricting, GOP State Senator Jay Morris yelled "Shut up, boy" to my Executive Director Dadrius Lanus, a Black man, who, in Sen. Morris’s words was “commenting and talking” too loudly for him to concentrate.
Sir, I am a 70 year old Black man and we know what it means to be called “Boy.”
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-louisianadems [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-louisianadems]
Senator Morris says we misheard. That the audio proves it. That he said “you all need to shut up” to the Black constituents behind him outraged that their votes won't be counted.
Senator Morris, an elected member of our legislature, thinks if he had yelled “you all need to shut up” it would be better.
It wouldn't.
What Senator Morris doesn’t understand is that White people have been telling Black folk to “shut up" for over 250 years.
What Senator Morris doesn’t understand is that we remember being told we were 3/5ths of a person. That even when we won personhood in the eyes of the law, they instituted poll taxes and “reading” tests. That when we marched and dreamed and cried and buried loved ones who had hung as strange fruit from tall trees because they raised their voices too loud that what Black people have always wanted is equality.
Or maybe Senator Morris does understand all that.
I don’t know.
What I do know is that I am a 70 year old Black man. And I don’t let anyone call me or my brothers “Boy.”
Please, chip in $10 or more today split between the Louisiana Democrats and Resist Reclaim Rebuild. Let’s show them that they may have gutted the Voting Rights Act and canceled our election, but we will not be silenced. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-louisianadems]

[**The Democratic Party is being remade in real time**](https://us.list-manage.com/Cn79C9_7BwZ?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)**, and most Americans haven't grasped what they just watched.**

| | 🔥 **MAMDANI GOES 3-FOR-3 — THE HOSTILE TAKEOVER IS REAL**
NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani's endorsed slate swept three NYC House primaries Tuesday. Some of the leftiest Democrats in Congress just got kicked out by socialists.
We walk through what these three candidates actually believe, and you'll understand why Scott Jennings says this should "frighten all Americans."

🚨 **A BROOKLYN COFFEE SHOP. A JEWISH CONGRESSMAN. THE SILENCE THAT FOLLOWED.**
The weekend before the primary, Dan Goldman walked into a coffee shop in Brooklyn. He was told he wasn't welcome.
He lost his race by roughly 30 points the next week.
Mamdani has said nothing about what's happening to Jewish Democrats in 2026. We have plenty to say.

| | 🏛️ **NO LIST. NO BALLOTS. NEW MEXICO IN THE CROSSHAIRS.**
The Postmaster General sat in front of the Senate Wednesday. Senator Gary Peters asked him one yes-or-no question about the proposed Trump rule on absentee ballots.
His answer should worry every New Mexican planning to vote by mail in November.
The comment period closes in days. Lawsuits are already moving. We break down what Steiner said, what it means for your ballot, and why the senators from Michigan and New Hampshire weren't satisfied with his answer.

🥇 **HAALAND PICKS HER OWN — MAYOR KEN GETS LOCKED OUT**
After Maggie Toulouse Oliver suspended her lieutenant governor campaign for health reasons, Deb Haaland made a move on the replacement process that has Republicans calling it the Kamala treatment.
Meanwhile, an independent gubernatorial candidate came up short on the 14,200 signatures he needed for the November ballot. We dug into how all 50 states actually pick their lieutenant governors, and you'd be surprised where New Mexico falls.

### This race is more important than ever, because a battle against the MAGA "patriot" facade exposes who really cares about Americans and their struggles.
Jun 28
---

You can't gerrymander your way out of $5 eggs. You can't AI post on Truth Social to change the billions gutted out of our healthcare system. Republicans in my district drew me out, but they didn't count on **that I would not back down.**
They are afraid of losing a seat to someone who actually shows up, talks straight, and refuses to play by the old rules. So they cracked communities, split neighborhoods, and shuffled the board to protect their own... **and put me against Scott Desjarlais.**_Yup, that guy._
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/72af2b31-8742-41c0-8351-52a91b0e40ed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Desjarlais stood by while data centers preyed on our communities and insurance companies spiked their rates. He voted to cut healthcare (while holding an M.D. himself) and slapped band-aid after band-aid on problems so MAGA would keep bankrolling him into office. _**That worked for 14 years, and it ends in November, as long as I have your help.**_
**👉 Please donate now because we deserve better than rigged maps and recycled politicians. [Start the wave of change this year by donating $20 HERE!](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/0510bc81-2ea7-4f83-b382-ee5b6f647f33?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[PITCH IN HERE!](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/0510bc81-2ea7-4f83-b382-ee5b6f647f33?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I'm not scared. I'm embracing the new 4th district because this is where I live, and that's where we continue this fight. The lines changed. **The mission didn 't.**
Working families in Middle Tennessee are still paying too much for groceries. Healthcare is still out of reach. Corporate interests still have more access to Congress than the people who elect it. **It isn 't a Tennessee thing, it's an America thing, because these agendas are Corporate level schemes, and this seat is the beginning of the end for them.**
This is exactly the kind of moment that separates candidates who are in it for the right reasons from those who aren't. I'm still here. Still knocking doors in every county they thought they could wall off.
Help us prove that the party tricks don't work when the candidate is willing to outwork everyone. _**[Your donation today goes directly toward building the ground game that wins this, county by county, neighbor by neighbor.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/0510bc81-2ea7-4f83-b382-ee5b6f647f33?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_

The Trump administration now has progressive activists in its sights, and is unleashing the full weight of the federal government to try and intimidate Democrats into silence.
| | | | | [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001_YzOZghkuwf9pW9BDwHhvP_tYpEYLXhpFaZgkduuaHl36QSezqSmPxoiPZsYeaAlclejUF0KN25Y8a7hf92Su2Qs_EBx3ZjiN4KjjjeWdR_E-nNjhUkeanaOw12DMoAibwIzyNhbpwNVLebHxa6ca92MXMqxwBX5dDg9qXBlyawj8WrUbtwl99SLmG-4T_V7iEwauaY_t4sTijvDYyUo2TyDOWjyBKOii0ykB8rFppvTKqxSjbea2w==&c=iMh9vJc5Movixj5elpg3rWC6SzVcmhRbNT4_BPGcBUQVsUx7ekqP0A==&ch=TXd6c4w0UXYugzeHKwOx90RPGYGB0Hzh5Q79W4IlI3vUbQpu-04Bbw==)

Peter,
Early this morning, the Department of Homeland Security conducted pre-dawn raids across Minneapolis, Minnesota and arrested 15 people on "conspiracy charges" for daring to protest ICE's occupation of the city earlier this year.
In a media release announcing the charges, DHS accused the protesters of being members of "ANTIFA"--a completely manufactured boogeyman MAGA invented to justify going after its critics, despite the fact that it isn't a real organization.
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001_YzOZghkuwf9pW9BDwHhvP_tYpEYLXhpFaZgkduuaHl36QSezqSmPxoiPZsYeaAlclejUF0KN25Y8a7hf92Su2Qs_EBx3ZjiN4KjjjeWdR_E-nNjhUkeanaOw12DMoAibwIzyNhbpwNVLebHxa6ca92MXMqxwBX5dDg9qXBlyawj8WrUbtwl99SLmG-4T_V7iEwauaY_t4sTijvDYyUo2TyDOWjyBKOi9vgiJJBI0xeXF1lfPGXwsg==&c=iMh9vJc5Movixj5elpg3rWC6SzVcmhRbNT4_BPGcBUQVsUx7ekqP0A==&ch=TXd6c4w0UXYugzeHKwOx90RPGYGB0Hzh5Q79W4IlI3vUbQpu-04Bbw==)
---
This comes on the heels of FBI raids on a prominent progressive voting rights organization in Ohio.
The Trump administration now has progressive activists in its sights, and is unleashing the full weight of the federal government to try and intimidate Democrats into silence.
None of this is happening by accident. Last fall, Trump signed something called NSPM-7--a presidential memorandum that claims to fight "domestic terrorism" and "political violence." In reality, it redefined opposition to Trump as terrorism. It directs the FBI's Joint Terrorism Task Forces to go after progressive activists, nonprofits, and the people who fund them. It even tasks the IRS with going after the donors behind movements Trump doesn't like.
The directive is explicit about who it's targeting: not violent criminals, but people with "extreme viewpoints on immigration," people who oppose this administration's policies, people who protest. This is a fascist crackdown and an assault on our First Amendment rights.
Democrats must fight back and save our democracy. Defend Our Courts is leading the defense. We are fighting on two fronts. First, building a firewall of state Supreme Courts with the power to protect free and fair elections state by state. Second, building the movement to reclaim the Supreme Court that has made itself an arm of the Trump administration.
Every day the Trump administration launches a new assault on democracy. We must stop them this November. clean_body: The Trump administration now has progressive activists in its sights, and is unleashing the full weight of the federal government to try and intimidate Democrats into silence. | | | | | == | Peter, Early this morning, the Department of Homeland Security conducted pre-dawn raids across Minneapolis, Minnesota and arrested 15 people on "conspiracy charges" for daring to protest ICE's occupation of the city earlier this year. In a media release announcing the charges, DHS accused the protesters of being members of "ANTIFA"--a completely manufactured boogeyman MAGA invented to justify going after its critics, despite the fact that it isn't a real organization. | == This comes on the heels of FBI raids on a prominent progressive voting rights organization in Ohio. The Trump administration now has progressive activists in its sights, and is unleashing the full weight of the federal government to try and intimidate Democrats into silence. None of this is happening by accident. Last fall, Trump signed something called NSPM-7--a presidential memorandum that claims to fight "domestic terrorism" and "political violence." In reality, it redefined opposition to Trump as terrorism. It directs the FBI's Joint Terrorism Task Forces to go after progressive activists, nonprofits, and the people who fund them. It even tasks the IRS with going after the donors behind movements Trump doesn't like. The directive is explicit about who it's targeting: not violent criminals, but people with "extreme viewpoints on immigration," people who oppose this administration's policies, people who protest. This is a fascist crackdown and an assault on our First Amendment rights. Democrats must fight back and save our democracy. Defend Our Courts is leading the defense. We are fighting on two fronts. First, building a firewall of state Supreme Courts with the power to protect free and fair elections state by state. Second, building the movement to reclaim the Supreme Court that has made itself an arm of the Trump administration. Every day the Trump administration launches a new assault on democracy. body:
Iran launched [a drone assault targeting Bahrain](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DHO4yAQBeDT2B0RDBhwQbFNumy7pTU243gSbEdAEmVP_8u5wl-ORnp63_t3GS7IibfrX1wp1HkfNnqXRLVSHjjjVmrmO5URl4y8VdzulHEACVZIK8APETl9BtPGMBMB6ZaCch6sURpkuwTQs3IjaO3HrosOZaeMt_3cdYYmJ1XL4UiTFryS0mt7itZj1N0YFfZWkmyMpMh1z6fbzltdaE6f_UX5NO1rm8JS66M0-k8D5wbO-DgAx-s4cuUpUQPngyKeRXDJSEm8MYtlz-vzvyg1I1dxe24kwImvLE7oNU1ydDCb3hOhU8bGudNKjbqf2hzi480pcbGuMfK6IqdvnfqrDV8BfgIAAP__rFaDqg), and a ship in the Strait of Hormuz also came under attack Saturday.

# Sunday, June 28, 2026
---|---
**Good Morning!** On this day in 1914, [Archduke Franz Ferdinand](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFygzAQAMDXiA5Gd8gyFCrS0DltSuaIDnO2kDxCtsa_zyRfyAe22K_LfCEJEq-ftLMra5oj1yNwKZxnyRSPkuXOx0JbJomF4p0zzajRttq2OMyeJLxn03i3MiP3DTs4D2gN9KibzS2se22tGQH1CAwnYCCwo8FxWc8GGnG_mrY4gNZDbztvB_L9afFAo9WsldHspaTc3ZLEsvEa3unFuftOexPcVsrjUP2HwknhVGvtysY15eAr5S7lq8IpMOWocKIlPUtbqyicbs_ILQ4tjGCa7PyjSghy2LMy-rqThD-__Cvl5fAnAAD__zXmdKk) and his wife, Sophie, were assassinated in Sarajevo by a Serbian nationalist group, setting off the chain of events that led to World War I. Jell-O enjoyed a steady build in American kitchens, from the Depression Era and World War II through its heyday in the 1950s. At its peak, the gelatin creations were the centerpiece of potlucks, but Jell-O's sugary profile eventually made it a prime choice for the _[Whatever Happened To...](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGuozAQAL_GdCCzGGMKF9fQ5dor0YKXsMmCI9sKyt-f8n7h9aMZaf7d5huy8Hn_iwf5ssX5pCsLlUJp5oRnLomflBfcE_JZ8HxSwhk02FrbGtwckOUzmyr4jQioq8i3gwNr2g50tfue9LAavdhhG8maMFA39GYMmxtXZ8xSsf_atAXXau062wTrMHT9ElocrSatjKbAJabmEfksO23yiW9KzRqPSvxeyiur7o-CScF0XVdz0FlQNok5fxkFE6bCq5CCyfYwuFbB9CCROtYZBUO9xRjqnXOJ6VMlH14Xi3C2gzL6fiDLT6v8atDbw_8AAAD__7i_ejQ)_ section.

**ICYMI:** Did you miss the Yale study that followed more than 11,000 seniors for over a decade? Researchers found that nearly half actually improved with age--not declined--and uncovered four hidden factor that made the difference. Which factors made the biggest difference? **Whatever happened to Jell-O?** For most of the 20th century, Jell-O was a powerhouse of American food culture, a product so embedded in everyday life that it seemed impossible it could ever fade. But fade it did, from the center of the dinner table to, well, mostly the hospital tray. The story began in 1897, when a cough-syrup maker named Pearle Wait and his wife, May, mixed fruit flavoring into powdered gelatin in their kitchen in Le Roy, New York. May coined the name Jell-O, but the couple couldn't figure out how to sell it and unloaded the trademark for just $450. The buyer, a local businessman named Orator Woodward, launched a national advertising blitz, and by 1902, sales had hit $250,000. The product took off during the Depression and World War II, when home cooks used Jell-O molds to stretch leftovers and dress up rationed ingredients. But the true golden age arrived in the 1950s. Gelatin molds became showpieces at dinner parties and potlucks, and women's magazines [published elaborate recipes](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOwjAQBNCvcTqjzcYxSeHimnRce2W0xBuy4NjItkD8_Qma-4ArR3qakebnNJ9IgsTLN-3s6prmyM8SuFbOs2SKpWa5cTnTlklipXjjTDMCWg1W4zB7kvCaTePdyozcNeza44DWtB1Cs7neAnfr2fp-xNWQNwscGdHDiDygaRtx7zawOLQAQ2cP3g7ku_7sWxotMCgD7KWmfLgmiXXjNbzSg_NhSXsT3FbrvajuS-GkcFqCLDfaOctCkd5E4ZR5kTsXhVOhQF7_5ZieRVfZWV85BJ30BxTdjj022fn7U0KQYo_KwGUnCZ_R-q-nHg5_AwAA__84Bn2R) calling for everything from shredded cabbage to tuna to hard-boiled eggs suspended in shimmering lime or lemon gelatin. Jell-O even released savory flavors, including celery, seasoned tomato, and Italian salad. On television, the brand's [catchy jingle](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuwyAQxvGnwVssODCmA0OlKlNTVerQbBYx5_gaAhG-xMrbV-4rdP0-6Tf8vw_DIVCifP4IV_Q8lSHjuiRkxjpQDXnhShdcTmGugTKHfMEaBpBgd9LuwA0xUHoOpol-QgTUDXrVO7BGaZDN7MfRTKbTYEBapWKHgHaSzvWm70ZQY0N-06QFp6R02rbRuhB1d4oqvFiJUhiJkbjU9qdQ5hmn9CwPrO1Yrk3yM_NtEfpVwF7Afl3X9lnufD_h9m9L4HEWev8Q-m1Ox8_jl33Hcm6qj7eVUqLF9sLI8zVQ-iP5Xx0eHn4DAAD__9IrcNw) became one of the most recognizable in advertising. It didn't last. By the mid-1970s, [savory Jell-O had fallen out of fashion](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGuozAQAL_GdCCzGGMKF9fQ5dor0YKXsMmCI9sKyt-f8n7h9aMZaf7d5huy8Hn_iwf5ssX5pCsLlUJp5oRnLomflBfcE_JZ8HxSwhk02FrbGtwckOUzmyr4jQioq8i3gwNr2g50tfue9LAavdhhG8maMFA39GYMmxtXZ8xSsf_atAXXau062wTrMHT9ElocrSatjKbAJabmEfksO23yiW9KzRqPSvxeyiur7o-CScF0XVdz0FlQNok5fxkFE6bCq5CCyfYwuFbB9CCROtYZBUO9xRjqnXOJ6VMlH14Xi3C2gzL6fiDLT6v8atDbw_8AAAD__7i_ejQ). Americans were paying more attention to sugar intake, Julia Child was reviving interest in traditional cooking, and more women were entering the workforce with less time for elaborate molds. The company pulled its savory varieties from shelves and pivoted hard toward marketing Jell-O as a treat for kids with Jell-O Pudding Pops, which lasted until the 1990s. A brief relaunch under the Popsicle brand in 2004 fizzled. By then, Jell-O had settled into a quiet existence as a budget dessert and a staple of hospital clear-liquid diets, where it provided calories and hydration to patients who couldn't eat solid food. Today, owner Kraft Heinz is trying to write a new chapter with last month's launch of Jell-O Simply, a line made with real fruit juice and 25% less sugar. And there's a small but [growing retro food revival](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGuozAQRb8GOiNjE8MWLrahe9tuiYbMOMzD2NHYCcnfr7K_8OorXZ1z_n4tX8CR0-0PHORryEuis0SqlWRhgVSq8E5lhU2AU4W0k8BitHFKO2WmBYHjexla9IHIkG3J9-Nk3NBbo9vNW7PCRQeNl0CjXYcwYRgRbQj2upJ2LfvPm3Zm6rWerOvQTYD2smIPv5wm3QyakGuW7jtzqhuF-M5Pku6ajzb6rdZ7aezvxsyNmc_z7EJ-fSw-e2PmkDMqFE57Y2ahKlkJBU6E6ptiVFkViICqwDPLW90oQuWkkMtGRR2wk3oket3pWgmVUH1IasXj_eQYubixGfTtAI7_eeqPIj69-RcAAP__QViKnA) on social media, where younger cooks are sharing gelatin "food art" on TikTok and Instagram, treating the jiggly creations as equal parts nostalgia and spectacle. It's a far cry from the shimmering centerpiece that once graced every church supper in America, but Jell-O is still wiggling. _Did you ever eat savory Jell-O salads growing up? That's why thousands are discovering Super Joint Support and its unique cartilage-supporting formula. See why Flyover readers are rushing to . | Whatever happened to Jell-O? For most of the 20th century, Jell-O was a powerhouse of American food culture, a product so embedded in everyday life that it seemed impossible it could ever fade. But fade it did, from the center of the dinner table to, well, mostly the hospital tray. The story began in 1897, when a cough-syrup maker named Pearle Wait and his wife, May, mixed fruit flavoring into powdered gelatin in their kitchen in Le Roy, New York. May coined the name Jell-O, but the couple couldn't figure out how to sell it and unloaded the trademark for just $450. The buyer, a local businessman named Orator Woodward, launched a national advertising blitz, and by 1902, sales had hit $250,000. The product took off during the Depression and World War II, when home cooks used Jell-O molds to stretch leftovers and dress up rationed ingredients. But the true golden age arrived in the 1950s. Gelatin molds became showpieces at dinner parties and potlucks, and women's magazines calling for everything from shredded cabbage to tuna to hard-boiled eggs suspended in shimmering lime or lemon gelatin. Jell-O even released savory flavors, including celery, seasoned tomato, and Italian salad. On television, the brand's became one of the most recognizable in advertising. It didn't last. By the mid-1970s, . Americans were paying more attention to sugar intake, Julia Child was reviving interest in traditional cooking, and more women were entering the workforce with less time for elaborate molds. The company pulled its savory varieties from shelves and pivoted hard toward marketing Jell-O as a treat for kids with Jell-O Pudding Pops, which lasted until the 1990s. A brief relaunch under the Popsicle brand in 2004 fizzled. By then, Jell-O had settled into a quiet existence as a budget dessert and a staple of hospital clear-liquid diets, where it provided calories and hydration to patients who couldn't eat solid food. Today, owner Kraft Heinz is trying to write a new chapter with last month's launch of Jell-O Simply, a line made with real fruit juice and 25% less sugar. And there's a small but on social media, where younger cooks are sharing gelatin "food art" on TikTok and Instagram, treating the jiggly creations as equal parts nostalgia and spectacle. It's a far cry from the shimmering centerpiece that once graced every church supper in America, but Jell-O is still wiggling. Did you ever eat savory Jell-O salads growing up? Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. subject: You probably remember that Paxton came after me and Powered by People in the middle of the Texas gerrymandering fight last year.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Powered by People, [poweredxpeople
body:
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=240916%2E444211%2Ew1fdT9)
If you want to end this MAGA nightmare... if you want James Talarico to be the next senator from the state of Texas... if you want to take it to Ken Paxton... this one is for you.
You probably remember that Paxton came after me and Powered by People in the middle of the Texas gerrymandering fight last year.
He sued us not because we’d broken any law, but because he hoped that bringing the full weight of the Attorney General’s office against us would cause us to throw in the towel. He was rightfully worried that our grassroots organizing, voter registration programs and our willingness to fight to the last breath against this attempted authoritarian takeover of our government would cause him problems in his race for Senate.
Maybe, he thought, he could tie us up in courts, force us to rack up unaffordable legal bills, and sideline one of the most innovative voter turnout programs in the country.
It’s what he’s tried to do to other groups across the state. Annunciation House. FIEL Houston. Catholic Charities of the Rio Grande Valley. Jolt Initiative.
He even sued the Democratic donation processing firm ActBlue.
Not because anyone has broken the law. But because he sees them as political opponents.
Here’s the good news. Like us, many of these groups are fighting back. And like us, many of them are winning. ActBlue just won a major decision in federal court.
That shows that standing up to a thug like Paxton, fighting back and fighting to win, works. So let’s keep it up. Because, while we’ve won at the district court and appeals court levels, he is not letting up, hoping to wear us down and stop us from organizing.
It hasn't been easy -- we’ve spent more than $500,000 in legal fees fighting him so far -- but it's been possible thanks to contributions from people like you.
[**Please donate today so that we can continue to beat him in court and focus on the work that will elect James Talarico the next U.S. Senator from Texas.**](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260628.rO-u17&refcode=ema20260628-240916&t=3&akid=240916%2E444211%2Ew1fdT9)

Thank you,
Beto

name: Alexander Vindman
subject: The Wall Street Journal
body:
I hope you can take a few minutes to read this.
# [](https://act.alexvindman.com/go/1113?t=1&akid=808%2E3892029%2EZj1UIN)

Peter: _The Wall Street Journal_ recently featured me in a new article. It talks about the urgency of the moment, and my ultimate decision to run for the United States Senate in Florida.
I’ve attached the article below. Thanks for taking a few minutes of your day to read it.
**[DONATE](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/avvf-digi-em-q22026?refcode=em260628-1&refcode2=808_3892029_Zj1UIN&akid=808%2E3892029%2EZj1UIN)**
* * *
**WSJ: Trump Whistleblower Eyes Senate Bid**
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/avvf-digi-em-q22026?refcode=em260628-1&refcode2=808_3892029_Zj1UIN&akid=808%2E3892029%2EZj1UIN)
_Alexander Vindman, key witness during Trump’s first impeachment, is vying for a Senate seat for Democrats_
-
On Jan. 12, Alexander Vindman had an “Aha!” moment: He saw a path to win the U.S. Senate race in Florida.
Sitting in his home office—surrounded by books in several languages, watercolors of his native Ukraine and a flag that flew over the U.S. Embassy in Moscow when he worked there—Vindman stared at political- polling research showing that he could win Marco Rubio’s former Senate seat.
For months, he had been frustrated. That month alone there was the capture of Venezuela’s President Nicolás Maduro, plus talk of taking over Greenland and Cuba. Then Renee Good was shot and killed by a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer in Minneapolis.
As the whistleblower for the first Trump impeachment inquiry in 2019, Vindman became a household name during his witness testimony, sitting upright in his Army uniform adorned with decorations. President Trump at the time called him “very insubordinate,” alleging Vindman leaked information and used poor judgment.
Now the 50-year-old former National Security Council analyst and retired U.S. Army lieutenant colonel wants to return to the Beltway—this time by making a long-shot bid for the U.S. Senate in solidly Republican Florida.
“The urgency of the moment could not possibly be greater,” he said in a recent interview in his home.
On the first day of his campaign, Vindman raised $1.7 million from more than 36,000 individual contributions, with 99% of online donations totaling $100 or less. On Wednesday, he announced that he has raised more than $8.2 million since launching his bid for Senate. He has almost a million followers on X.
Still, “as much money as he will raise, he is easy to frame as a partisan Democrat who was a driving force behind impeachment,” says David Wasserman, an elections analyst with the Cook Political Report.
Vindman faces a primary in August against other Democrats, including state Rep. Angie Nixon. The winner will face Republican incumbent Ashley Moody, the Trump-endorsed former Florida attorney general, who was appointed by Gov. Ron DeSantis after Rubio resigned to become U.S. secretary of state.
Many political observers see an uphill battle for Vindman, despite his national profile. Florida has shifted from purple to deep red in recent years, thanks to demographic changes, political organizing and the disarray of the Democratic Party’s infrastructure.
Yet some see cracks in the state’s red wall. In December, Miami elected its first Democratic mayor in nearly 30 years. And last month, Democrats flipped two state legislative seats in special elections—a senate seat in Hillsborough County and, in the night’s biggest shocker, a house seat in Palm Beach County—home to Trump’s own Mar-a-Lago—against a candidate personally endorsed by the president.
Vindman’s challenge will be much harder, because he is running for a statewide office, says Cook’s Wasserman.
To win, he said, Vindman will need Democratic voter turnout to outnumber Republicans. He will also need to win unaffiliated voters by a 2-to-1 majority and to win a small slice of Republicans, Wasserman says.
Vindman believes he has better odds. “People are eager for a different direction,” he said at a recent campaign event at the Collier County Democratic headquarters in Naples. He was met with shouts of “Amen!”
**A family decision**
When Vindman first told his wife of 20 years, Rachel Vindman, that he wanted to run for office, she said no—vehemently.
“I can’t express how adverse I was to this idea,” she says. “We had done our part, and then some. Why would we do this again?”
Rachel, a political activist who is co-chair of the Veterans and Military Families Council of the Democratic National Committee, understood that her husband’s campaign would put her family back in the spotlight. After the impeachment trial, she said, came lies, personal attacks and death threats, even against their daughter. Elon Musk tweeted that Vindman had committed treason.
To discuss the potential run, the couple took a drive through the Everglades. There was talking—and yelling. (“My wife is a fiery redhead; I was lucky to return,” Alex says.) He explained his motivation to his wife—that he believes that there is a chance to win Florida and he is the one to do it.
She asked him if it would harm their marriage if she refused to let him run, and he said no. Then she said yes to a campaign. “Service is the most important thing to him,” she says. “I didn’t want him to ever feel that he didn’t do what he needed to do.”
**American dream**
Born Jewish in Soviet-era Ukraine—both of Vindman’s grandfathers died fighting the Nazis—he lost his mother at age 3. The next year, his father immigrated to the U.S. with Vindman and his two brothers, arriving on Christmas Day with just $759. Vindman’s twin, Eugene, is now a Democratic U.S. representative from Virginia and their older brother, Leonid, works as an investment banker.
Vindman spent 21 years as an Army infantry officer, military strategist and diplomat. He served in South Korea, Germany and Iraq, where he earned a Purple Heart for wounds from an improvised explosive device attack.
He then transitioned into diplomatic work, rising to become a top Russia strategist for the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. He eventually joined the White House’s National Security Council as director of European affairs.
Alexander Vindman testifying before the House Intelligence Committee during a public impeachment hearing.
It was in that role that Vindman sat in the White House Situation Room in 2019 and listened to the now-famous call in which Trump asked his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky to “look into” then-Democratic presidential candidate Joe Biden.
Vindman says that his military training and sense of duty made him report that call. In a twist of fate, the NSC attorney he reported it to was his brother, Eugene, who was the chief ethics official for the staff at the time.
The House approved two articles of impeachment against Trump in 2019. Trump denied any wrongdoing and he was later acquitted by the Senate. Two days later, Vindman and his brother Eugene were fired from the NSC and escorted out of the White House by security. Vindman retired from the Army in 2020, citing a campaign of retaliation against him that he said included stalling his promotion to full colonel.
Seeking a change of scenery, Vindman and his family relocated to the Sunshine State three years ago. He moved his father and stepmother down, too, paying half the rent in their retirement community so they can live nearby. “I love it here,” he says, “but what fool moves to Florida if they thought they might run for statewide office?”
On the campaign trail, Vindman talks about wanting to “end the chaos, crush corruption and cut costs.” At the event at the county Democratic headquarters in Naples, he was welcomed like a returning war hero.

WSJ: Trump Whistleblower Eyes Senate Bid Alexander Vindman, key witness during Trump’s first impeachment, is vying for a Senate seat for Democrats - On Jan. 12, Alexander Vindman had an “Aha!” moment: He saw a path to win the U.S. Senate race in Florida. Sitting in his home office—surrounded by books in several languages, watercolors of his native Ukraine and a flag that flew over the U.S. Embassy in Moscow when he worked there—Vindman stared at political- polling research showing that he could win Marco Rubio’s former Senate seat. For months, he had been frustrated. That month alone there was the capture of Venezuela’s President Nicolás Maduro, plus talk of taking over Greenland and Cuba. Then Renee Good was shot and killed by a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer in Minneapolis. As the whistleblower for the first Trump impeachment inquiry in 2019, Vindman became a household name during his witness testimony, sitting upright in his Army uniform adorned with decorations. President Trump at the time called him “very insubordinate,” alleging Vindman leaked information and used poor judgment. Now the 50-year-old former National Security Council analyst and retired U.S. Army lieutenant colonel wants to return to the Beltway—this time by making a long-shot bid for the U.S. Senate in solidly Republican Florida. “The urgency of the moment could not possibly be greater,” he said in a recent interview in his home. On the first day of his campaign, Vindman raised $1.7 million from more than 36,000 individual contributions, with 99% of online donations totaling $100 or less. On Wednesday, he announced that he has raised more than $8.2 million since launching his bid for Senate. He has almost a million followers on X. Still, “as much money as he will raise, he is easy to frame as a partisan Democrat who was a driving force behind impeachment,” says David Wasserman, an elections analyst with the Cook Political Report. Vindman faces a primary in August against other Democrats, including state Rep. Angie Nixon. The winner will face Republican incumbent Ashley Moody, the Trump-endorsed former Florida attorney general, who was appointed by Gov. Ron DeSantis after Rubio resigned to become U.S. secretary of state. Many political observers see an uphill battle for Vindman, despite his national profile. Florida has shifted from purple to deep red in recent years, thanks to demographic changes, political organizing and the disarray of the Democratic Party’s infrastructure. Yet some see cracks in the state’s red wall. In December, Miami elected its first Democratic mayor in nearly 30 years. And last month, Democrats flipped two state legislative seats in special elections—a senate seat in Hillsborough County and, in the night’s biggest shocker, a house seat in Palm Beach County—home to Trump’s own Mar-a-Lago—against a candidate personally endorsed by the president. # Just The Truth
Your No-BS Newsletter ``` Dear Readers, Today’s sponsor, Eduardo Verástegui and the Sound of Freedom Foundation, is supporting efforts to combat child trafficking through prevention training, community outreach, and educational programs designed to help protect vulnerable children before exploitation occurs. Thank you for your consideration of our sponsors.
The Just The Truth Team
* * *
GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE Friend,My name is Eduardo Verástegui.I am the producer of the film _Sound of Freedom_ and founder of the **Sound of Freedom Foundation.** Years ago, after hearing firsthand stories about children trapped in trafficking, my life changed forever.What I learned broke my heart.Children were being bought and sold. Exploited. Abused. Forgotten.And most people had no idea this evil was happening all around us.That is why I made the film _Sound of Freedom_.**Not for Hollywood.
Not for awards.
But because I believed people needed to see the truth.**[](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/lq7Yj3S4tkzRFUK4maHBlSTzA7aVcBNRkXB%2FFJal8q5bOxTX2FoRWwPhXsmF%0AlnMRTD6SU9gi%2FXCN1OwmR%2F%2BGDJhGgE8HJ0PSUT8ay4DA%2B6oTC2RBx7VGyDiM%0Ak3hFBdquOXVT%2FlA%2BRpAM0cCi8cr%2BI8pYIKS8cS31W86rwJ6O9SJLkjU1RSTA%0AVrYMv%2FK2SNUFw2kfoT%2BLyC2pwY%2BeZQ7XSw%3D%3D%0A/cb4ef5f9f5ea3a3c)Today, the **Sound of Freedom Foundation** continues that mission beyond the movie screen.[ Help Stop Child Trafficking ](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/fQd5sVPAuxZUIx1kEVysrnYFc0VkoGLVHBwjVGcbZNlho3Tzm%2FitQQ5YYcUR%0AAGjLSbmAO4XbyQRgQW6F083kWjJCdUKO%2B96%2FTAcg5i5OaOGVyEAL5X%2Bn7zsb%0A2UR6avFx55XbyIfQ9M%2FogFJu0OptROdaQvOSPFunn4uqFCMOOCQpBLi0VuPj%0A9OEVWGdmasrSLT73oGZMYwjGjQ4UXBNOTw%3D%3D%0A/954c1614714bbb8d)**We exist to stop the sale of God’s children.** And right now, we are urgently preparing for a major threat connected to the premier international soccer tournament coming up in June and July.Millions of visitors will flood into 16 cities across the United States, Mexico, and Canada.While families gather to celebrate soccer, traffickers often use large international events like this to exploit vulnerable people, especially children.[ Help Stop Child Trafficking ](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/91xKp6a%2FvuoIG5GPiuJgr5v09l3E33HzQf7BiDVa%2FBGgEc7X8HgEH2BepVKt%0AXuOaxyk0ZQ2d7C9RN%2Fz3HYpUHE6IG9tjM6mFNEb2VfMISXWSSqcXCjmMwFDa%0AXHj2ux0NOLxGZCL30rOwnqD2bBf3szborgeP5qsXpdRposbBtoePxJJb7YP2%0AnpI1teqhmoJT3egNfixvz16Icm8YvpLf0Q%3D%3D%0A/c2c6fd472b83d07b)That's why survivor-informed community groups and anti-trafficking leaders are mobilizing before the games begin.Volunteers and community partners will gather with **Sound of Freedom Foundation** partners to take action against traffickers.This collaborative effort will provide:
* Trainings and presentations
* Outreach opportunities
* Community toolkits designed to help prevent trafficking before, during, and after the tournament

Survivors of trafficking themselves will help lead these trainings.They will prepare volunteers to reach hotels and motels near tournament activity zones with prevention resources and awareness materials.**Because awareness saves lives.
Education protects children.
Staying silent helps traffickers.**[](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/KsuElYoXGZSHXVOz7Aa7UmYjnZYf15nBgzHWASPHttlk5MecXBq022w3A4mI%0AtTjCsK1TxkLHtf8qu7SSIaug7NZ8wnnBEdd4bggO1xi5w8u22ZVXeYBS52o6%0Ax8WTbxkRhv7lFqDsNlvpkdfcWCZonLZkv8IlP5Q9LOeVNpvHDPSzzZa0Q%2FNg%0ACDkhPgDNwpVURH29EFv7g1ryIO3Rpof%2Bqg%3D%3D%0A/9ea406127d89af9a)[ Help Stop Child Trafficking ](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/Ah77CPCuhcCgfxneVc3yPabCowqdFXFjpSxMkbVyOecEcZYTg%2FMwTU6zFck4%0ABTBu5xQ8nlw2UB1gRK8wwSsFxjqvPQGsvzUKuGKIpXpnqgerLp%2BO%2BQ5RTa0l%0AZKGtU2u9HUZrYnKZaLvBWjXGnbwVej2WcNGjBAPMfW6A8eg0VY2u9fM0QFI5%0ApOFlF3hjXN0I3wIJhoRf2YAOB0aUmSZf%2BQ%3D%3D%0A/74341d2f2628b1bf)The **Sound of Freedom Foundation** supports efforts like these because prevention is one of the most powerful ways to stop exploitation before it begins.Jesus said:_“Whoever welcomes one such child in my name welcomes me.”_ (Matthew 18:5)**I believe protecting children is not optional.
It is our responsibility.**[Friend, will you make your first gift of $25, $50, $100, or whatever you can give today to help protect vulnerable children from trafficking during the tournament and beyond?](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/yQeV1eAcKumazcv7lpDd38NsmAIUnmalMmg35OokiSqSMuLC9i5gI1gfKNB6%0AnJEeyfnw0T8gAlEEWapRvR4Of8kVYLoYobsQoJzgUyLCFCAJmc7CfY8Zy3dY%0A0nT5RRZ1IfnSVvigiYbaXrLOUNIB0LyzRHikWW5MsCSefIhcIzir%2Bcs06ubw%0AM%2FrJdcEk5gD6rPT12jnciQv4WcvR48I2fw%3D%3D%0A/fa1c83e408d29118)Your gift today can help support:
* Survivor-informed trafficking prevention trainings
* Community education and awareness efforts
* Outreach resources for hotels and high-risk areas
* Prevention tools that help communities recognize trafficking before it happens

**Your support of $25, $50, $100 or any amount can help protect children who are vulnerable right now.** When good people stand together, darkness loses its power.Please join us today in this mission of life.**Because God’s children are not for sale.** With gratitude and prayer,[](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/HzkU3TjhYg0Y2ZsmcYUZUjanKT9hvccYQ6%2BDHrP600IkQXAwSqW6Uwqo1k5G%0AT2TJCcWNVoK5WNMtiR6jzP66cKvi%2BJimaLOcC2yNetVatTTqEIGlgRCiGduO%0Al5s62N3oektBkb6oSD8g7x5aNC1tVqI9mXcDeBCOTEAZvCTNUDWcttJzD11w%0A1obdcWqLjFAmqVoJ8du4N%2Fndg1iVJazBFw%3D%3D%0A/afd5074318b66da1) Eduardo Verástegui

name: Roy Cooper (via Cooper Victory Fund)
subject: You deserve to know the truth
body:
This is what it’s going to take to win what’s expected to be the most expensive Senate race in U.S. history.
|
# [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/6532?source=&t=1&akid=1913%2E124072%2EdAKvAK)
| | | |
---
Hi there, Peter –

Since we have just over 48 hours left until our FEC end-of-quarter deadline, at the end of this email, I’m going to ask you to chip in $5 to my Senate campaign in North Carolina.
If you’re short on time, though, and want to have an immediate impact in our fight to flip this toss-up seat, **[you can chip in here now.](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk713&amount=5&t=8&akid=1913%2E124072%2EdAKvAK)**
**You deserve an explanation for today’s request:**
June has been a huge month for our campaign. We went up on TV with our first ad, new polls came out showing this race moving further and further in our direction and, although the GOP doesn’t like it, momentum is clearly on our side.
That’s because of you. I’m grateful for the hundreds of thousands of folks who’ve joined our movement to end the GOP’s one-party rule and return power to working families.
**However, it’s been very challenging too.** A major far-right super PAC launched a new six-figure ad buy attacking me – bringing total GOP investments in this race so far to _$100 million_ , and Peter, that’s just the beginning.
Republicans know as well as we do that the path for Democrats to retake the Senate majority runs straight through North Carolina – and they’re throwing everything at the wall to defeat us. The only way I can fight back against this onslaught of dark money is with grassroots support from folks like you.
**[That’s why I need your help to reach the $1.5 million goal I set for Tuesday’s public fundraising deadline. It’s our most ambitious goal yet, but it’s what we need to raise if we’re going to win what’s expected to be the most expensive Senate race in U.S. history. Please, will you chip in $5 to help win this battleground race and retake the Senate majority?](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk713&amount=5&t=9&akid=1913%2E124072%2EdAKvAK)**
_If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | | | [DONATE $5](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15913?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk713&amount=5&t=10&akid=1913%2E124072%2EdAKvAK)
---
| | [DONATE $25](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15913?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk713&amount=25&t=11&akid=1913%2E124072%2EdAKvAK)
---

---
With your help to close the gap, we won’t just be able to compete with the GOP’s massive spending – in the end, we’ll prove that their well-funded efforts to crush our grassroots movement were futile.
Thank you.

Roy Cooper
| |
* * *
[](https://act.roycooper.com/go/8188?t=2&akid=1913%2E124072%2EdAKvAK)
Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

subject: America’s 250th birthday
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the National Democratic Redistricting Committee, John Bisognano, President
body:
It’s our turn to strengthen the fabric of our nation.

---
Peter, America will celebrate its 250th birthday next week. It can be easy to overlook just how incredible — and improbable — this milestone is. America has always been an experiment, defined by the belief that people united not by race or ethnicity but by a shared set of ideals can live and work together. We’ve seen the power of that belief over the last two and a half centuries. But our democracy has never been self-executing. At every turn, we’ve had to keep it alive. Revolutionaries, inventors, abolitionists, suffragists, civil rights leaders, entrepreneurs, and organizers have worked and sacrificed to keep us moving forward. Of course, there have always been people who don’t believe in the American experiment — leaders who put their self-interest ahead of the common good, and would prefer to take us backward rather than give up their own wealth and power. But generation after generation, the American people have prevailed. They’ve rolled up their sleeves, locked arms, and done the hard work of building a more perfect union. **Now it’s our turn to answer the call. ** **The National Democratic Redistricting Committee has a plan to defeat the gerrymandering that threatens fair elections so we can ensure that the will of the people ultimately prevails. We celebrate this historic milestone because it took heroism and sacrifice to get here. It took leaders who had a vision for what America could be — and who helped make it real.
Together, they believed in an America where everyone has an equal opportunity to make their voices heard. Where every person is equal under the law, no matter who they are or where they live. Where elections are always free and fair.
**250 years after America’s founding, that vision is still our north star. Attorney General Eric Holder and I founded the NDRC to protect the promise of America from the extreme, anti-democratic forces trying to undermine it.**
Right now, too many Republicans are trying to hold onto power and silence voters. They’re manipulating district maps to entrench themselves, while making it harder for ordinary citizens — especially in Black and brown communities — to elect the representatives they want.
**But in America, we the people get the final say. It’s our turn to roll up our sleeves and help strengthen the fabric of our nation.[I believe we will rise to meet the urgency of this moment. clean_body: It’s our turn to strengthen the fabric of our nation. Peter, America will celebrate its 250th birthday next week. It can be easy to overlook just how incredible — and improbable — this milestone is. America has always been an experiment, defined by the belief that people united not by race or ethnicity but by a shared set of ideals can live and work together. We’ve seen the power of that belief over the last two and a half centuries. But our democracy has never been self-executing. At every turn, we’ve had to keep it alive. Revolutionaries, inventors, abolitionists, suffragists, civil rights leaders, entrepreneurs, and organizers have worked and sacrificed to keep us moving forward. Of course, there have always been people who don’t believe in the American experiment — leaders who put their self-interest ahead of the common good, and would prefer to take us backward rather than give up their own wealth and power. But generation after generation, the American people have prevailed. They’ve rolled up their sleeves, locked arms, and done the hard work of building a more perfect union. Now it’s our turn to answer the call. The National Democratic Redistricting Committee has a plan to defeat the gerrymandering that threatens fair elections so we can ensure that the will of the people ultimately prevails. = | If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: = | = = | = = | = We celebrate this historic milestone because it took heroism and sacrifice to get here. It took leaders who had a vision for what America could be — and who helped make it real. Together, they believed in an America where everyone has an equal opportunity to make their voices heard. Where every person is equal under the law, no matter who they are or where they live. Where elections are always free and fair. 250 years after America’s founding, that vision is still our north star. Attorney General Eric Holder and I founded the NDRC to protect the promise of America from the extreme, anti-democratic forces trying to undermine it. Right now, too many Republicans are trying to hold onto power and silence voters. They’re manipulating district maps to entrench themselves, while making it harder for ordinary citizens — especially in Black and brown communities — to elect the representatives they want. But in America, we the people get the final say. [4,316,233 babies were born in the United States](https://substack.com/redirect/f1b80f76-7ec7-4c97-8aec-8f6447120e59?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) during 2007, the most in American history. The fertility rate, a measure of how many children are born per woman, stood at 2.12, almost exactly at the level needed to keep the population stable.
All of that seemed to change in 2008. When Lehman Brothers collapsed on September 15, 2008, the birth rate collapsed along with it. The number of births in America had already started slipping earlier in 2008 (~68,000 fewer babies than the year before) but by 2009, births had [dropped to 4,131,000](https://substack.com/redirect/f1b80f76-7ec7-4c97-8aec-8f6447120e59?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (~185,000 below the 2007 peak.) And it just kept falling. Through the recovery, through the bull market, through the lowest unemployment in half a century. Year after year after year.
Last year, [3.6 million babies were born](https://substack.com/redirect/8d9d61e3-6f99-4bea-9fec-8c49501f14ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg); that's **700,000 fewer than the 2007 peak**. The fertility rate hit [another record low: 1.6 children per woman](https://substack.com/redirect/fa2f53cf-f2c9-4441-b93e-1c26514928a0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), well below the replacement rate, and government demographers believe it will stay near 1.6 [through 2055](https://substack.com/redirect/1f4bb866-10e6-4b3f-8298-6a8978388e07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/cb882a3d-365c-44df-8f4d-f0c596e03d77?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Photo by [Levente Varga](https://substack.com/redirect/1a716455-73ef-4c61-a77c-6b5e310a20c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on [Unsplash](https://substack.com/redirect/ad64fa14-4533-46d8-978e-a85c37493180?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
But let's consider the demographic ripple this change in birth rate is causing. What about all those babies that weren't born in 2009? All those missing babies translates into missing adults now. They would have been turning 18 next year. They're the first cohort of the "missing generation" and they're absent from college enrollment lists, military recruiting pools, and entry-level job applicants.
Between 2008 and 2025, roughly **7.4 million fewer Americans were born** than would have been at the 2007 rate. That's 7.4 million fewer workers, taxpayers, consumers, soldiers, and Social Security contributors. They don't exist and no policy can create them retroactively.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..JUJcfNhqxUZA3RG6LR0dehiG0WpPmDmV3Gqzcx9-r5E?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=203853563)
The demographics were screaming. The elementary school classrooms got emptier every year. The middle schools followed. Then the high schools. And now the empty chairs have finally reached the college lecture halls as enrollment is falling off a cliff.
Syracuse University's chancellor just [told faculty the school will run its first budget deficit in years](https://substack.com/redirect/da4a5df8-7b39-453f-80b7-ee4bf943ab40?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) because it can't fill its freshman class. The school [cut 93 academic programs](https://substack.com/redirect/c9354a1a-bed3-4421-a3da-ef6a7299a767?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg); 55 of those had zero enrolled students. To attract the ones who do exist, Syracuse offered [tuition discounts of up to $200,000](https://substack.com/redirect/175f5561-c35d-413c-a110-54b248d95441?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to students who'd already turned them down. Syracuse isn't alone. Ohio State cut eight majors and merged 20 others. The University of North Texas slashed 70 programs amid a $45 million deficit. The University of Chicago paused doctoral admissions in over a dozen humanities departments. Demographers call it the ["enrollment cliff,"](https://substack.com/redirect/4929b9d3-ff56-4a86-89c9-5542571d6d17?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a projected 5 to 10 percent decline in freshman class sizes beginning now.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/8bce584e-c176-43b2-9b94-449974143185?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Just as colleges are missing students, the Pentagon is missing soldiers. The U.S. Army missed its [FY22 goal by 25% and its FY23 goal by 10%](https://substack.com/redirect/1cddc769-5497-4a38-87db-360b7d68c2a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). This rebounded a bit after the services raised the enlistment age to [42](https://substack.com/redirect/c2438273-96a5-49fe-9b1c-2335d5fd5c76?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), loosened drug and tattoo restrictions, and created a [pre-boot-camp prep course](https://substack.com/redirect/ddeaa183-76a8-4468-8171-ee3f51f0259c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to get unqualified applicants up to standard. But the math is about to get worse. The [Hoover Institution projects](https://substack.com/redirect/1cddc769-5497-4a38-87db-360b7d68c2a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a **10% reduction in eligible 18-year-olds starting in 2026** , directly caused by the post-recession birth decline. And of that shrinking pool, [only 23% are eligible to serve](https://substack.com/redirect/1cddc769-5497-4a38-87db-360b7d68c2a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) without a waiver; the rest are disqualified by obesity, mental health issues, drug use, or criminal records. Center for a New American Security projects a [13% decline in 18-year-olds between 2025 and 2041](https://substack.com/redirect/d4085d5a-7aa1-4dc9-ab76-78aa4daf05f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). You can't recruit soldiers who don't exist.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/be7f4dc2-d6c9-48cb-a4a5-ea4f0e695177?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
In addition to working its way through colleges and the military, the demographic ripple is about to hit the workforce. Fewer 18-year-olds means fewer entry-level workers in a labor market that's already tight. And fewer consumers. It means fewer first-time renters, fewer people buying their first car, fewer consumers forming households and spending money in the ways that drive economic growth. It's also important to note that these dynamics mean fewer workers will be paying into Social Security, the retirement system supporting 70 million retirees who seem to be living longer and longer. Might the baby bust lead to Social Security's collapse?
The 2008 financial crisis broke something that 18 years of recovery couldn't fix. The economy came back. The stock market hit all-time highs. Unemployment fell to historic lows. None of it mattered. The birth rate just kept falling, through boom years, low-unemployment years, stimulus years, wage-growth years. Once a generation loses confidence that the future will be better than the present, the babies don't come. And once they don't come, you can't get them back. The last full-sized cohort of 18-year-olds is walking across graduation stages right now. Next year, the missing generation arrives. Or rather, doesn't.
The baby bust is going to reorder our society in ways that we are only beginning to understand. And as the BBC video below describes, this is not just a US story.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/b530bc0c-ad4f-4c41-918e-a38afd3d821d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The implications of fewer humans on the planet are likely to be disruptive and lead to many changes, but it's important to be balanced in our thinking. Yes, fewer workers may lead to higher wages and a wage-price spiral, but might the dynamic also allow for the rapid introduction of artificial intelligence without social disruption or unrest? Yes, fewer humans may result in an "enrollment bust" with our inflated education industry, but perhaps an aging population might find fancy campuses more suited to retirement communities?
My main point here is not that the baby bust is good or bad, but rather that it's an under-the-surface demographic trend that will have major implications for various industries and the economy as a whole. And in times like these, it's critical we spend time connecting dots across seemingly irrelevant domains (aging populations and college campuses, for instance) to unveil lurking risks and spot hidden opportunities.

Once a generation loses confidence that the future will be better than the present, the babies don't come. And once they don't come, you can't get them back. The last full-sized cohort of 18-year-olds is walking across graduation stages right now. Next year, the missing generation arrives. Or rather, doesn't. The baby bust is going to reorder our society in ways that we are only beginning to understand. And as the BBC video below describes, this is not just a US story. The implications of fewer humans on the planet are likely to be disruptive and lead to many changes, but it's important to be balanced in our thinking. Yes, fewer workers may lead to higher wages and a wage-price spiral, but might the dynamic also allow for the rapid introduction of artificial intelligence without social disruption or unrest? Yes, fewer humans may result in an "enrollment bust" with our inflated education industry, but perhaps an aging population might find fancy campuses more suited to retirement communities? My main point here is not that the baby bust is good or bad, but rather that it's an under-the-surface demographic trend that will have major implications for various industries and the economy as a whole. And in times like these, it's critical we spend time connecting dots across seemingly irrelevant domains (aging populations and college campuses, for instance) to unveil lurking risks and spot hidden opportunities. Hey Peter!

It’s Katie, Abdul’s Finance Director. Today, I want to pull back the
curtain on something most campaigns never talk about.

The closer we get to Election Day, the more obsessively we watch our cash
flow. I’m talking daily check-ins on what we can *actually* afford.

More ads? Maybe. Another GOTV rally? We’d love to. More resources for our
field team? Always on the wish list.

If the budget gets tight, then we’ll be forced to start cutting back.
That’s the stressful part. 😅

Most campaigns don't sweat it like this. When there's a gap, they pick up
the phone, call a corporate PAC or AIPAC, and the problem disappears in
exchange for blind loyalty.

We refuse to do that because Abdul is sticking to his values. He’s never
taken corporate PAC money or pandered to AIPAC, and never will. That’s a
huge reason why I’m so proud to be a part of Team Abdul!

But at the end of the day, we’re staring down a primary flooded with $30+
million in AIPAC spending. The only way we’ll overcome that mountain of
cash is by banding together.

To avoid scaling back our campaign efforts, we set a goal of raising $1
million through emails like this one before Tuesday night’s FEC deadline.
It’s a big bet, but Abdul fully trusts that members of this team will step
up and support us through the final stretch.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260628-1-ak.f9H_Rk&amount=10&refcode=em20260628-2464&t=1004&akid=2476%2E251025%2Eq7b_P- ]Can we count on you,
Peter? Donate $10
or any amount to help us meet our goal before Tuesday night:

Thank you, thank you, thank you!

Katie
Finance Director

subject: Only 2 Days Left Before Our FEC Deadline
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Committee to Elect Enoch, Catherine Johnson, Treasurer
body:
We have just TWO DAYS left before our Federal Election Commission fundraising deadline.

| | | | | |
---
| | | | |
---
| | Hello Peter,
We have just **TWO DAYS** left before our Federal Election Commission fundraising deadline.
This is one of the last public reports voters, the media, and political insiders will see before our campaign enters the next phase. Every contribution made before the deadline sends a clear message that the people of Ohio's 8th Congressional District are ready for new leadership.
Washington has become a place where wasteful spending is treated like business as usual.
Think about this: the federal government has now spent **more than $16 million** on the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool renovation—a project that ended up making headlines after the pool turned green with algae instead of delivering the promised results.
Imagine what $16 million could have done for real families.
That same amount of money could have provided the equivalent of **one full year of income at the federal poverty level for approximately 485 families of four.** Instead of lowering costs for working families...
Instead of strengthening Social Security...
Instead of improving our schools...
Instead of helping veterans...
Instead of making healthcare more affordable...
Congress continues to tolerate waste while too many families are struggling to pay for groceries, rent, childcare, and prescription medications.
I'm running for Congress because our priorities are backwards.
Every taxpayer dollar should be treated with respect. Government should invest in people—not waste, political theater, or projects that fail to deliver results.If you're tired of seeing your tax dollars wasted while Congress refuses to act, I'm asking you to stand with our campaign today.
Please make a contribution before our FEC deadline in just **two days.**
Whether it's [$10, $25, $50](https://enochforcongress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=488c703b71891f0b712737c99&id=12550a18eb&e=c6e7dff14c), or whatever you can afford, your contribution helps us build a campaign that answers to the people—not special interests.Together, we can demand accountability, restore common sense, and fight for a government that works for working families again.
Thank you for believing that change is possible.
With gratitude,
**Dr. Vanessa Enoch**
Democratic Candidate for Congress
Ohio's 8th Congressional District
**P.S.** After the FEC deadline passes, our fundraising totals become public. Let's show Washington that the people of Ohio's 8th District are ready to replace wasteful politics with accountable leadership. Please donate before midnight in two days.
Paid for by the Committee to Elect Enoch, Catherine Johnson, Treasurer.

subject: I Started Working at 14. Here's What I Learned.
body:
A carpenter. A builder. A man who knows what Tennessee needs. | | | [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMUOS4HeVvfmscBPlPRAgpkDEziezgtKrXjuDy5eJDcjRJNOVndPp-iRW-yHbE22q-wgMttH4O70fDCtXDjWtuoqGpE85Gn-EENtQSJ7r9JxIZbk7hAfJGHXvd5HpPmBR55Sd6jf6jH9bH4tkxPVePgaRa7InCHwo_oQZSaVvbFHj51Dk5uOni4o7qEIMcDbjZzzOQ47mTCMj9QBZXbBL9nwjzbyMo0j_Mn4ofZ8Od8KvxfnuAH3XKyzn8GvYEqbs1Vc1dJZQd2Ne3JJSHi4HCmTNLvF5vycM7DbhnXEZrDrM/4rv/tNFSipE9SMK1AeHMxPdTsg/h0/h001.zXQI5ISFjnaxcksxUAQdpBZ_sWYh_Xej7laJtJCIeRM)
Friend, I want to tell you what I saw. I grew up on a farm and started working in construction at 14. By the time I graduated high school, I could read blueprints and frame a house from the ground up. After studying at the University of Kentucky, I dedicated myself to becoming a General Contractor. At 29, I started my own corporation. Nothing was handed to me. Everything came through hard work and dedication. Over the years, my company completed projects across Middle Tennessee. We built sorority houses, apartment complexes, tiny homes, and custom built-ins. We built things to last. **Every structure depends on its foundation.** The same is true for our communities. What I saw was a workforce being overlooked. Young people who need practical skills and real opportunities. An industry that needs trained workers. Communities that need more housing. Construction costs rising and projects getting delayed because there are not enough skilled workers entering the trades. That is why workforce training matters. We need to invest in carpentry, plumbing, welding, crane operation, heavy equipment, and safety training. Once people learn a skill, they carry it for a lifetime. What I saw also changed the way I think about housing. We need homes built to last. We need to think carefully about the materials we use, the way we design communities, and the way we move materials. Did you know construction accounts for fifty percent of worldwide pollution? When we train workers better, we build more efficiently. Better construction means less waste, lower costs, and more opportunity for people who want to build a future for themselves and their families. **Women make teams better.** I have seen safety improve. I have seen communication improve. I have seen efficiency improve. My wife transformed our timekeeping and budget tracking. My sister became an excellent trim carpenter. Those experiences taught me the value of bringing more people into an industry that needs talent and leadership. Workforce training. Affordable housing. A cleaner earth. These are challenges I have spent my life working around, thinking about, and trying to solve. clean_body: A carpenter. A builder. A man who knows what Tennessee needs. | | | Friend, I want to tell you what I saw. I grew up on a farm and started working in construction at 14. By the time I graduated high school, I could read blueprints and frame a house from the ground up. After studying at the University of Kentucky, I dedicated myself to becoming a General Contractor. At 29, I started my own corporation. Nothing was handed to me. Everything came through hard work and dedication. Over the years, my company completed projects across Middle Tennessee. We built sorority houses, apartment complexes, tiny homes, and custom built-ins. We built things to last. Every structure depends on its foundation. The same is true for our communities. What I saw was a workforce being overlooked. Young people who need practical skills and real opportunities. An industry that needs trained workers. Communities that need more housing. Construction costs rising and projects getting delayed because there are not enough skilled workers entering the trades. That is why workforce training matters. We need to invest in carpentry, plumbing, welding, crane operation, heavy equipment, and safety training. Once people learn a skill, they carry it for a lifetime. What I saw also changed the way I think about housing. We need homes built to last. We need to think carefully about the materials we use, the way we design communities, and the way we move materials. Did you know construction accounts for fifty percent of worldwide pollution? When we train workers better, we build more efficiently. Better construction means less waste, lower costs, and more opportunity for people who want to build a future for themselves and their families. Women make teams better. I have seen safety improve. I have seen communication improve. I have seen efficiency improve. My wife transformed our timekeeping and budget tracking. My sister became an excellent trim carpenter. Those experiences taught me the value of bringing more people into an industry that needs talent and leadership. Workforce training. Affordable housing. A cleaner earth. These are challenges I have spent my life working around, thinking about, and trying to solve. That is why I am running for Congress. I build things that last. Thank you for being part of this campaign. 💙 Love y'all, Tim Lanier Candidate for Congress, Tennessee's 4th District | | | ---|---|--- | | Sent via . Friend — it’s Ilhan.
As you probably know, our FEC fundraising deadline is just two days away.
[**I’m humbly asking for your support before then. Please, hear me out.**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-jun26.ltbpUI&refcode=em260628-1-210&t=3&akid=2315%2E791427%2EwMe8sY)

This has never been easy.
I survived a civil war, was raised in a refugee camp, immigrated to the US, and found a good life in Minnesota. I got active in my community and eventually earned the privilege of serving and representing my neighbors in Congress.
Since then, I’ve faced attacks and harassment from some of the most powerful people in the world; the President, the Vice President, leading members of Congress, foreign leaders, billionaires, AIPAC, right-wing media outlets and corporations, you name it.
I’ve dealt with the endless death threats, the insults, the people who think I’m not good enough, or not ‘from here’, and want to see me deported or worse.
**But through all of this, I’ve never backed down. Because I have YOU.**
This team and the movement we’ve built together have helped me push through and keep up the fight for the dignity of all Americans.
Because our progressive vision for this nation, where everyone is taken care of and provided the basic human rights and fair shot that they deserve, is worth fighting for, despite it all.
So, with this crucial FEC deadline coming up fast, I’m counting on you to stand by my side as you always have.
[**I’m humbly asking you to make a contribution of $10 or whatever you can afford today. Do it before our deadline comes and we close the books on our fundraising report.
