After Tuesday’s deadline, two things are going to happen:
**FIRST, my team and I are going to make a big decision.**
On Wednesday morning, we’re going to sit down and look at our fundraising numbers for the quarter. If we meet our end-of-quarter goal? That’s our green light to scale up our efforts and keep investing in efforts to reach undecided voters and protect this district.
But if we fall short? That’s a sign that we need to seriously consider reorganizing our funds — and that means less digital ads online, fewer undecided voters reached, and ultimately, _less momentum for this campaign._
**THEN, our fundraising numbers are going to go public. **
That means that anyone — _including our general election opponents_ — can take a look at our fundraising numbers for this quarter. They’re going to be poring over our data, looking for any sign of vulnerability or weakness in this campaign that they can exploit and use to defeat us in November.
**But if we meet our fundraising goal, they won’t find a single one.**
That’s why Tuesday’s deadline is so important — because our ability to defend Oregon’s 6th District is on the line.

name: AOC
subject: I won't give up.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
If we do not assert ourselves and enshrine our rights — and demand healthcare, and education, and dignity — the alternative is barbarism, which is what we are contending with now.
The fact that people are choosing between medicine and rent is barbarism.
The fact that people are worried about whether they will be on the streets every 4 weeks is barbarism.
The fact that every time a person has an ache or a pain, and they’re scared that it could either be a sore joint or cancer, but they can’t find out because they can’t afford the doctor? **This is barbarism.**
If we do not demand — and not only demand, but win — unions, healthcare, wages, and ending endless war, then we will condemn ourselves to barbarism.
I refuse to give up. I refuse to submit myself to that future. That’s not a life.
**And so to live, we have to fight for each other. We have to stand with each other. We have to fight for this vision and this world.**
[If you can, will you make a $5 contribution – or any amount that is meaningful to you – to help power our fight for transformative change? Every donation will make a difference, and help me defeat my MAGA opponent this November.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260628.6CpAUl&refcode=em20260628-11824-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=11824%2E2526796%2EIKwShH)

Now let me tell you why this mission means so much to me. My name is Eduardo Verastegui. Several years ago, I learned firsthand about the horrific reality of child trafficking. What I heard broke my heart. Children were being bought and sold.
Families were being torn apart.
Lives were being destroyed. **I couldn't forget it.** **I couldn't stay silent.** I kept asking myself one question: **"What if it were my child?"** That question changed my life. What started as a film project became a mission and a calling. That calling eventually led me to help produce the film _Sound of Freedom_. **Not for fame.**
**Not for awards.**
**But because I believed people needed to see the truth.** For years, many people said the film would never succeed. Doors closed.
Studios walked away.
People told us to give up. **But when innocent children are suffering, silence is not an option.** And while the film helped awaken millions of people to this crisis, awareness alone is not enough. That is why we created the **Sound of Freedom Foundation**. Our mission is simple: **To stop the sale of God's children.**

People who believe children deserve safety, refuse to look away and are willing to stand up and say: "No more." Every time you wear it, you'll be sharing a message that matters. A message that reminds the world that every child has God-given dignity. And importantly, a message that sparks conversations and helps raise awareness about a crisis many people still do not see. Most of all Friend, I hope this shirt reminds you that you are part of something bigger than yourself. A growing movement of people determined to protect vulnerable children. Please accept this shirt as our way of saying thank you for joining this mission. Give any amount today and choose your shirt size and select a color. What I heard broke my heart. Children were being bought and sold. Families were being torn apart. Lives were being destroyed. I couldn't forget it. I couldn't stay silent. I kept asking myself one question: "What if it were my child?" That question changed my life. What started as a film project became a mission and a calling. That calling eventually led me to help produce the film Sound of Freedom. Not for fame. Not for awards. But because I believed people needed to see the truth. For years, many people said the film would never succeed. Doors closed. Studios walked away. People told us to give up. But when innocent children are suffering, silence is not an option. And while the film helped awaken millions of people to this crisis, awareness alone is not enough. That is why we created the Sound of Freedom Foundation. # [Thank You for Your Support!](https://bethfarnhamforcongress.com/2026/06/28/thank-you-for-your-support/?jetpack_skip_subscription_popup)
---
By **Elizabeth Farnham** on June 28, 2026
---
| **District Round-up 06.28.26**
---
Dear Neighbor, Thank you for reading my District Round-up. As your candidate for Pennsylvania’s 13th Congressional District, it is my honor and pleasure to deliver to you where I’ve been and what issues I’ve tackled in the past week. Criss-crossing the counties of Adams, Franklin, Fulton, Bedford, Cambria, Blair, Huntingdon, Mifflin, Juniata, Perry, Cumberland, and Somerset gives me great opportunities to meet with voters, hear what is on your hearts and minds, and the chance to voice my fight for Everyday Americans. If you would like to contribute to my campaign, please donate here:**[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/beth-farnham-for-congress-1](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=68ba75fac504fd63468e01dc21c1892573474569119da16610336d020c010367&blog_id=213069660&post_id=7968&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=75152f41f718b79bf390b1265fa860d3&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYWN0Ymx1ZS5jb20vZG9uYXRlL2JldGgtZmFybmhhbS1mb3ItY29uZ3Jlc3MtMQ=&email_id=42c527e214ae7dedc0e505df50a2b6b0)**
---
| **Announcing Campaign Headquarters!**
---
| |
---
Because of your generosity, Team Beth Farnham for Congress has been able to lease office space for the campaign for the next 5 months.
---
This is our opportunity to streamline processes like postcarding, fundraising, getting out the vote, and more in order to get Beth Farnham into Washington DC to represent US!
---
Drop in anytime between 2 PM – 4 PM on Wednesday, July 1st, in order to learn about how you can help Beth’s campaign. Enjoy some light refreshments, bask in the great lighting, revel in the cool air conditioning, and have fellowship with others who want Beth Farnham to win this seat in Congress.
---
**If you would like to sign up as a volunteer now** , simply click on the pink “Join Us!” button at the top of this page, or click on the link below: [https://bethfarnhamforcongress.com/welcome-volunteers/](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=ded2db1880414794669cbd736fdb32c08ec94fc90654c06fb1b015f757e8187a&blog_id=213069660&post_id=7968&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=43f357f8f53520c7693d57650f59864a&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly9iZXRoZmFybmhhbWZvcmNvbmdyZXNzLmNvbS93ZWxjb21lLXZvbHVudGVlcnMv&email_id=42c527e214ae7dedc0e505df50a2b6b0)
---
If you are already a volunteer, stop in anyway! We’d love to see you!
---
Together, we Choose Democracy!
---
| **Gettysburg Groundbreaking**
---
| |
---
| |
---
It was a great day on Monday in Gettysburg for the groundbreaking of Dobbin House Square.
---
Many thanks to Education Forward for their generous donation of life-size replicas of the Declaration of Independence, the United States Constitution, the Bill of Rights, Civil Rights Amendments, and the Gettysburg Address.
---
The words of these historic documents are precious to our Democracy and belong in the public spaces so new generations can be inspired.
---
Together, we #ChooseDemocracy!
---
| | **Recession Indicator!**
---
Are your credit card balances rising? You’re not alone.
---
As a former credit analyst tasked with evaluating risk in order to increase or reduce credit lines, the increasing American credit card debt amount feels quite, quite familiar.
---
Not only is the national collective credit card balance nearing its 2011 peak of $1.25 trillion, but the delinquency rate is approaching that of the Great Recession 2010 peak of 13.7%.
---
That means that nearly $171.3 billion worth of credit card debt is 90 days delinquent or more.
---
Unsurprisingly, across several social media posts, credit card holders with stellar (self-reported) credit scores are posting credit line reductions on their cards even though they pay on time.
---
Indeed, it is a general practice of financial institutions to reduce credit lines of consumers, despite their excellent credit history, in order to reduce risk because banks don’t know who will all of a sudden run up this form of unsecured debt. History has shown that even people with good credit scores will put large amounts of debt on their credit cards when facing a financial crisis.
---
While gas prices have come down about $.14 since Trump’s Memorandum of Understanding with Iran, they’ve been so high for so long, people have had to resort to packing on the credit card debt to get by. And Trump isn’t helping the situation every time he threatens this tentative peace. Moreover, Iran still maintains the power to close the Strait of Hormuz.
---
Meanwhile, according to Consumer Price Index data, the cost of groceries has continued to rise 2.9% over April 2025.
---
And so hard-working families and retirees on a fixed income turn to their credit cards to make ends meet, then begin to fail to pay them.
---
Of course, our own U.S. Representative, multimillionaire John Joyce says nothing about the financial stress Americans are suffering under Trump. Instead, he poses for a picture with his foot on the stairs of Air Force One because he just admires Trump so much.
---
But it doesn’t have to be this way.
---
We can fire Joyce by electing me, Beth Farnham, to US Congress on November 3rd because I actually care about Everyday Americans and would ensure, along with other caring legislators, liveable wages and social safety nets so Americans would not have to burden themselves with overwhelming debt and suffer poor credit scores.
---
Together, we #ChooseDemocracy and financial health!
---
(Pic of food pantry, My Neighbor’s Bounty, in Mercersburg, Franklin County, PA)
---
| |

| **Meet and Greet in Perry County!**
---
Many, many thanks to Dr. Kim Boyer and Dr. Bill Sisson for hosting their fabulous meet and greet in Perry County and for each personally endorsing my campaign.
---
I truly appreciate the opportunity to engage with voters over the issues that are near and dear to our hearts – from uncapping contribution amounts of the ultra-wealthy toward social security in order to ensure solvency of the social security funds and dignity in our final years, to healthcare that insures all, to meeting the needs of our farmers, to halting the cruelty of the Trump administration, it was a great question and answer session.
---
I’m also deeply honored that Bill brewed a delicious American Wheat Ale and named it after the campaign.
---
Together, we #ChooseDemocracy and Community!
---
| |

| | |

| **Medicare/Medicaid Fraud!**
---
| |
---
Medicaid/Medicare fraud absolutely exists, but the perpetrators are more often the providers, not the beneficiaries.
---
“Federal prosecutors said the beneficiaries and physicians listed on the fraudulent claims had never heard of Oregon Clinical Laboratory and the genetic testing was never provided.”
---
In Pennsylvania, State Attorney General, Dave Sunday, filed charges yesterday against eight people who committed fraud too.
---
“Armstrong submitted time entries for more than one Medicaid consumer at the same time, and she was paid $70,0332 for services she did not provide, according to investigators.”
---
This is because the Medicaid/Medicare money doesn’t go to the beneficiaries directly, but to the ambulance companies, pharmacies, hospitals, nurses, doctors, home health agencies, and a whole host of providers.
---
Yet, our own US Representative, multimillionaire John Joyce, voted to take away healthcare from 17k constituents because he falsely claims they defrauded the system.
---
Without any proof of wrongdoing, Joyce damned the poorest people of our 13th Congressional District into even poorer health.
---
Meanwhile, again, because he and others like him signed the One Big Beautiful Bill Act that ended covid era subsidies for Pennie, the Affordable Care Act (Obamacare) of Pennsylvania, over 145k Pennsylvanians whose monthly Pennie premiums leapt up by several hundred dollars per person have dropped their insurance.
---
Instead of helping Everyday Americans, the Trump administration is hell-bent on hurting them.
---
But it doesn’t have to be this way.
---
You can elect me, Beth Farnham, to fire Trump, Vance, RFK Jr, other civil officials, and Supreme Court Justices so that we don’t simply exist, but thrive. I’ll work with other caring legislators to create a national healthcare plan so no American goes without coverage.
---
Why?
---
Because healthcare is a human right and the richest country in the world can foot the bill, instead of paying for costly and unjustified wars in Iran, or deportation of asylum seekers.
---
Together, we #ChooseDemocracy and Good Health!

Many thanks to Education Forward for their generous donation of life-size replicas of the Declaration of Independence, the United States Constitution, the Bill of Rights, Civil Rights Amendments, and the Gettysburg Address. The words of these historic documents are precious to our Democracy and belong in the public spaces so new generations can be inspired. Together, we #ChooseDemocracy! | | Recession Indicator! Are your credit card balances rising? You’re not alone. As a former credit analyst tasked with evaluating risk in order to increase or reduce credit lines, the increasing American credit card debt amount feels quite, quite familiar. Not only is the national collective credit card balance nearing its 2011 peak of $1.25 trillion, but the delinquency rate is approaching that of the Great Recession 2010 peak of 13.7%. That means that nearly $171.3 billion worth of credit card debt is 90 days delinquent or more. Unsurprisingly, across several social media posts, credit card holders with stellar (self-reported) credit scores are posting credit line reductions on their cards even though they pay on time. Indeed, it is a general practice of financial institutions to reduce credit lines of consumers, despite their excellent credit history, in order to reduce risk because banks don’t know who will all of a sudden run up this form of unsecured debt. History has shown that even people with good credit scores will put large amounts of debt on their credit cards when facing a financial crisis. While gas prices have come down about $.14 since Trump’s Memorandum of Understanding with Iran, they’ve been so high for so long, people have had to resort to packing on the credit card debt to get by. And Trump isn’t helping the situation every time he threatens this tentative peace. Moreover, Iran still maintains the power to close the Strait of Hormuz. Meanwhile, according to Consumer Price Index data, the cost of groceries has continued to rise 2.9% over April 2025. And so hard-working families and retirees on a fixed income turn to their credit cards to make ends meet, then begin to fail to pay them. Of course, our own U.S. Representative, multimillionaire John Joyce says nothing about the financial stress Americans are suffering under Trump. Instead, he poses for a picture with his foot on the stairs of Air Force One because he just admires Trump so much. But it doesn’t have to be this way. We can fire Joyce by electing me, Beth Farnham, to US Congress on November 3rd because I actually care about Everyday Americans and would ensure, along with other caring legislators, liveable wages and social safety nets so Americans would not have to burden themselves with overwhelming debt and suffer poor credit scores. Together, we #ChooseDemocracy and financial health! (Pic of food pantry, My Neighbor’s Bounty, in Mercersburg, Franklin County, PA) | | | Meet and Greet in Perry County! Many, many thanks to Dr. Kim Boyer and Dr. Bill Sisson for hosting their fabulous meet and greet in Perry County and for each personally endorsing my campaign. I truly appreciate the opportunity to engage with voters over the issues that are near and dear to our hearts – from uncapping contribution amounts of the ultra-wealthy toward social security in order to ensure solvency of the social security funds and dignity in our final years, to healthcare that insures all, to meeting the needs of our farmers, to halting the cruelty of the Trump administration, it was a great question and answer session. subject: What it means to be a Tennessean.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Molder for Congress
body:
Practical common sense. Kindness. A shot at success for everyone. That is Tennessee.

| | | | |
---
Peter,
I have been thinking a lot lately about what it means to be a Tennessean.
It means common sense. It means kindness. It means wanting to live in a community where everyone has a shot at success. It means sweet tea on the front porch, talking with neighbors. It means being able to disagree with our neighbors respectfully, but recognizing that as Tennesseans, we agree on the important stuff.
Those are not Democratic values or Republican values. They are Tennessee values, and I have seen them everywhere I have traveled across this new district.
[](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/YKTWKGncuqITpBK2yO7txQ~~/AAUS1hA~/OsC9RUkvJfW0jShJYxteaKLWH3fEH1--MGiWuV2YCwGcr5599_r0kisMN_8_Or3b4E12g1vJdlwNf4h2JuPLAUNy8EzVeHcF-GX8UkYj5k3bNe1OnMCajmVibtg9mqG7qJvtblMkowIEzIXynTU1mNdVQfkzA5Y2VPKUNHAjLj69EYqY9sN3qEJMYryPRNyejeJ8qMxgJCjR_Im_qiNW18tHGvhXkTtP9EU-GzfYLKw-zcpypRKuQn5Pg6dCgn_J)
This November, we have a chance to prove that Tennessee is ready to send a little decency to Washington. Someone with Tennessee roots who understands that we are united by far more than what divides us. Someone who knows that serious times call for adults in the room.
Andy Ogles is not that person. He has proven it over and over again. But this race is winnable, the momentum is real, and the end of the quarter is our chance to show everyone watching that Tennessee is ready for something better.

clean_body: Practical common sense. Kindness. A shot at success for everyone. That is Tennessee. | | | | | Peter, I have been thinking a lot lately about what it means to be a Tennessean. It means common sense. It means kindness. It means wanting to live in a community where everyone has a shot at success. It means sweet tea on the front porch, talking with neighbors. It means being able to disagree with our neighbors respectfully, but recognizing that as Tennesseans, we agree on the important stuff. Those are not Democratic values or Republican values. They are Tennessee values, and I have seen them everywhere I have traveled across this new district. This November, we have a chance to prove that Tennessee is ready to send a little decency to Washington. Someone with Tennessee roots who understands that we are united by far more than what divides us. Someone who knows that serious times call for adults in the room. Andy Ogles is not that person. He has proven it over and over again. A few weeks ago, my husband and I lost a pregnancy.
The physical toll was something not even my doctor prepared me for.
After 11 weeks of hope about bringing a new member into our family, we learned the pregnancy was no longer viable. After several weeks of bleeding and mourning, my doctor made clear that future pregnancy could be much more difficult if I didn't take medication to expel the retained miscarriage.
Like most women, I was told the medication would feel like a regular period. Maybe a little stronger cramping.
But when I took the medication, the pain was more intense than the pain I experienced delivering my son four years ago. I wasn't even advised to take it when my son was out of the house.
And I am not alone.
Women are routinely told that Ibuprofen is sufficient pain management during miscarriage. In practice, that's the functional equivalent of handing someone a stick to chew on.
Science and medicine have advanced in so many ways, but when it comes to reproductive health, the standard of care for women's pain in this country is still medieval.
I know there are broad differences in beliefs about reproductive health. But we do not need to agree on every policy question to agree that women should not have to endure excruciating pain while managing a miscarriage and protecting their ability to go on and bring a child into this world.
One in four women will likely experience a miscarriage. We can do better than telling them to take Ibuprofen and endure it.
That's why I introduced and passed a simple amendment directing the NIH to study strategies to improve pain management during miscarriage.
If you agree that women deserve better pain care than the status quo provides and that the Senate should pass this amendment, add your name today. [https://go.marieforcongress.com/a/women-pain-care]
ADD YOUR NAME [https://go.marieforcongress.com/a/women-pain-care]
We don't need to agree on everything to agree on this: Women who lose a pregnancy deserve compassion and dignity.
Thank you,
Marie

I grew up on a cattle ranch and television isn’t my pastime. Being a husband and a father are the two most important things in my life. Sometimes, when I'm holding my kids I feel like I'm holding the whole world in my arms. **They are the wind in my sails when it comes to the mission I’ve committed my life & career to. ** And at the end of my life, I want to sit before the Father almighty and declare that I did all I could to leave this great country better off than it was when I grew up. _**[Nothing – I repeat – nothing is more important to me than fighting off the vicious leftist attacks against the soul of our country.](https://links.iterable.com/s/c/uBVCx1XaczIcf38O1p3aNK0C63qCjE53QhPdfJv8Lmihfswm9MF8-gLl0vTW8wX8l-03QslVjdpvwoe4rwOeTiLEgZwBV8jhsFwJKWjH68VThiTV51g9Z19zpUTMzUdmV3Qcxmcspq51Ho8I2HE00LGTjwO0fUD9lHFFhkXQxVOhZaoVcuO4pCxftYMGpqsVAyx_uq_ozH2hz5gpAuh0Z0kgD0sEcNr-ax42oFZUZFnORsGXVLfnunl7-SgkOJQX-X_eAyW3w8FCm-aucB_CYDOrSjhy5NSAVUsRkP0kTHykjmybRbkLYvJkfGOetLO9HUXuiBSR1CK9PVm8dpABiU87ki-7pgJ6mIQ9xN-Pbws148TqqhTorAvJ_w0D9oKlfm91flr75SZ_9F_0GhqDWGONgTZcDB_jAFljgVHYYGNgfkUaXnL9DKATR3aUBXW7MkXPma-eGxYfXRAd_l1yBIjR2pm1gCWq6ImsxvluX3apFyxTND8cYGnxoDbaPpcGsuU4e_FDKoBF05h0j6gjOs03Pz_3IXA7lG06qWr2IP0qUxQaBz7MHRoF6KFZqDv0IaMwua_qZnjL7bOkIiXx7Z4H31fZgYFR3gBXMV38vRmtRDGzVYCX8rlzt097Ebbnn6TAn-QyueONK4L3BJPGZiOQy8TAG6ha7pUnUHvtWV2yJorYyg9jlaRdl-j1yanvPsg5d5kKgB7wUSwidryYxwrptQn_bCZ7CqYCAtp8IAkVb9y3vFusLtjcX6eLep5VMsctf4HRJGJBs_Yd-58EVEPm22f7tmJVAZl-OI0YQ2HckD5aNQ/6mVu94kCitiRx8eyN0clItUnq_sYwFDX/22)**_ The left hates you, they hate your vote, and they hate MAGA for putting America First. name: J. Davis
subject: The farming accident that changed my life
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JAMIE DAVIS FOR U
body:
August 8th, 2008, the worst day of my life, changed how I see everything: from family to the importance of our rural communities and it is a key part of why I am running for office.
| | | | | [](https://kseax8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001j-1PQmcu6AwMww9hYD_A5WCzAvAzNPZ2CD1kt9bevLC1_-XscLv4c3zwk_3ORp7HIS7GtmS-ze4pPzyJJPHmTkBMivQV1K1at0NhYA3pAlR4f_7AVnLwnL9-kyyQWr5Z4GLnHmDMfb1kMkUM1Drqm53rbhMKVmdH3JucrbNZtibKI0m3gyegEdstz_C4G3aUH8F6EFEVlrxy_fx3Gg9pp6Fzidi7Rrr0FQ4h1mvARCs=&c=byFc6le4-qniJlUFKCOjPNxK34Vzdn1kP9UP4z57oGQg_5RemzvyuA==&ch=oKaOCUp-Vk8SEKnadbh7zh5Dlx2TX3xC36Y89lhYuDVQQ7Fy1_hiLA==)
---
Peter,
August 8, 2009, is a date I will never forget.
Just days before his 19th birthday, my son Justin was out in the fields with us, doing what this family has done for over three generations--farming the Louisiana delta. A breakdown in our combine left corn spilled across the ground, and as we worked to recover it, Justin got too close. In an instant, his pant leg was caught, and the thresher pulled him in.
I can still hear his voice: "Dad, get me out."
And there was nothing I could do.
---
| [](https://kseax8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001j-1PQmcu6AwMww9hYD_A5WCzAvAzNPZ2CD1kt9bevLC1_-XscLv4c3zwk_3ORp7HIS7GtmS-ze4pPzyJJPHmTkBMivQV1K1at0NhYA3pAlR4f_7AVnLwnL9-kyyQWr5Z4GLnHmDMfb1kMkUM1Drqm53rbhMKVmdH3JucrbNZtibKI0m3gyegEdstz_C4G3aUH8F6EFEVlrxy_fx3Gg9pp-AfpPV0xo-MWUN2m1WRviQ=&c=byFc6le4-qniJlUFKCOjPNxK34Vzdn1kP9UP4z57oGQg_5RemzvyuA==&ch=oKaOCUp-Vk8SEKnadbh7zh5Dlx2TX3xC36Y89lhYuDVQQ7Fy1_hiLA==)
---
My son and I on the farm in 2021.
Multiple miracles occurred that day: When it initially happened he wasn't in pain because his nerves were pinched so tightly in the machine. Nor was he bleeding because he was caught so tight in there.
It took the jaws of life to tear apart that machine and when the metal finally gave way he let out a scream that I will never forget for the rest of my life.
The paramedics quickly sprang into action and he was airlifted to Jackson, Mississippi, where Doctors fought to save his leg, but the injury and infection from all the dirt and debris were too severe. Justin lost his leg from below the knee.
That day could have broken us. Instead, it showed me what makes Louisiana strong.
Neighbors, first responders from two parishes (what we call counties in Louisiana), and a doctor who wasn't even on duty, Dr. Ron Gregg, a farmer himself and longtime family friend -- showed up because that's what rural communities do. They take care of each other. They don't ask if it's their job or jurisdiction. They just show up.
Today, Justin is 35. He runs our farm. He's built a life, with a fiancee and a family of his own. He still hunts, fishes, and works the land -- just with a prosthetic leg and the same determination that carried him through that day.
But the truth is, the kind of community that saved Justin is disappearing. Rural hospitals are closing. Doctors like Dr. Gregg--who live in our communities, who know our families--are harder to find. Too many of our kids feel like they have to leave home to build a future.
And my family, who first worked this Louisiana delta soil as sharecroppers, and now as farmers who own this land, have put too much blood into this soil for us to leave and go somewhere else.
I have to take a stand and fight for our way of life. That's why I am proud to be the Democratic Nominee for US Senate in Louisiana.
If you believe in this fight, I'm asking you to stand with me today. A Democratic win here is the first step in taking our state back from the far-right whose policies of atomization and vicious corporatism are tearing our communities apart.
And mark my words, a win is possible! We WON our runoff election last night by a landslide! [The blue wave will wash over Louisiana and we will flip this seat but only if we fight for it. Will you please make a contribution of $50, $25, or even just $5 to help us in our fight to restore the Louisiana that we love so dearly.](https://kseax8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001j-1PQmcu6AwMww9hYD_A5WCzAvAzNPZ2CD1kt9bevLC1_-XscLv4c3zwk_3ORp7HyE16kQ3oWHRLANb1klGifHD6RHiRX6ctBdFZSv75eKIu7dmrgMUzDJsXsQduXE7OeGHkIS37For37NyteV0F2xc68RlVKZAXiNUGTL_CzNLxKCOVwgI19Pk-1DBmN6l8T4md8Qv9xVOgsXAATwneTCm6DFB7qSl0S7e_YXrFpL6qaa1BcNAxqA==&c=byFc6le4-qniJlUFKCOjPNxK34Vzdn1kP9UP4z57oGQg_5RemzvyuA==&ch=oKaOCUp-Vk8SEKnadbh7zh5Dlx2TX3xC36Y89lhYuDVQQ7Fy1_hiLA==)

clean_body: August 8th, 2008, the worst day of my life, changed how I see everything: from family to the importance of our rural communities and it is a key part of why I am running for office. | | | | | == Peter, August 8, 2009, is a date I will never forget. Just days before his 19th birthday, my son Justin was out in the fields with us, doing what this family has done for over three generations--farming the Louisiana delta. A breakdown in our combine left corn spilled across the ground, and as we worked to recover it, Justin got too close. In an instant, his pant leg was caught, and the thresher pulled him in. I can still hear his voice: "Dad, get me out." And there was nothing I could do. | == My son and I on the farm in 2021. Multiple miracles occurred that day: When it initially happened he wasn't in pain because his nerves were pinched so tightly in the machine. Nor was he bleeding because he was caught so tight in there. It took the jaws of life to tear apart that machine and when the metal finally gave way he let out a scream that I will never forget for the rest of my life. The paramedics quickly sprang into action and he was airlifted to Jackson, Mississippi, where Doctors fought to save his leg, but the injury and infection from all the dirt and debris were too severe. Justin lost his leg from below the knee. That day could have broken us. Instead, it showed me what makes Louisiana strong. Neighbors, first responders from two parishes (what we call counties in Louisiana), and a doctor who wasn't even on duty, Dr. Ron Gregg, a farmer himself and longtime family friend -- showed up because that's what rural communities do. They take care of each other. They don't ask if it's their job or jurisdiction. They just show up. Today, Justin is 35. He runs our farm. He's built a life, with a fiancee and a family of his own. He still hunts, fishes, and works the land -- just with a prosthetic leg and the same determination that carried him through that day. But the truth is, the kind of community that saved Justin is disappearing. Rural hospitals are closing. Doctors like Dr. Gregg--who live in our communities, who know our families--are harder to find. Too many of our kids feel like they have to leave home to build a future. And my family, who first worked this Louisiana delta soil as sharecroppers, and now as farmers who own this land, have put too much blood into this soil for us to leave and go somewhere else. I have to take a stand and fight for our way of life. That's why I am proud to be the Democratic Nominee for US Senate in Louisiana. If you believe in this fight, I'm asking you to stand with me today. A Democratic win here is the first step in taking our state back from the far-right whose policies of atomization and vicious corporatism are tearing our communities apart. And mark my words, a win is possible! body:
The establishment knows what a win here would mean.
#
Hi Peter,
This week, my fellow Justice Democrats-backed Democratic socialists won BIG in New York.
Anti-corporate PAC, anti-AIPAC, pro-working-class candidates defeated establishment-backed opponents and proved voters are tired of being told to settle for Democrats who talk about defending democracy while protecting the same billionaires, lobbyists, and war machines that are doing active harm to working people here at home and funding a genocide abroad.
Now, the next test is in Denver this Tuesday.
I’m Melat Kiros, a Democratic Socialist running for Congress in Colorado’s First Congressional District against a corporate-sponsored incumbent who has been in office for 30 years.
The establishment knows what a win here would mean. It would mean our movement is not confined to New York, and working people across the country are ready to elect someone who will fight for Medicare for All, universal child care, housing as a human right, an arms embargo, and a government that answers to us instead of corporate PACs and weapons manufacturers.
It would mean another reliable vote for the status quo is **gone**.
And that is exactly why they are panicking.
On Thursday, a dark-money Super PAC with reported ties to AIPAC announced they are spending more than $1 million in the final days of this race to stop us from defeating my corporate-sponsored opponent.
They are flooding Denver with anonymous money because they know I cannot be bought.
I was fired from my job as an attorney after I refused to take down a statement defending students who were speaking out against the genocide in Gaza, and in Congress I will not be silent while our government sends bombs instead of investing in working families.
They know I will not take corporate PAC money, bow to AIPAC, or give billionaires a veto over what our communities deserve.
That is what this race is about. The political establishment wants to prove New York was a fluke.
We have the chance to prove it was the beginning of something much bigger.

Melat

Peter,
Following the passage of the 14th amendment in 1868, anyone born in the United States is a citizen of the United States.
Since then some of America's greatest innovators and leaders became citizens thanks to this. Even Nikki Haley, the daughter of two immigrants from India, became a citizen thanks to birthright citizenship, and supports it.
However, within the first day of Trump's 2nd term, the President signed an executive order to throw out this precedent. Within 24 hours the order was challenged and a hold was placed on it but now the Supreme Court is set to rule on the fate of this American cornerstone.

If their ruling to strike down abortion or to reinstate Jim Crow voter discrimination are any indication, we should be deeply worried about how the Supreme Court plans to rule on birthright citizenship.
If they strike down this fundamental American right, millions of leaders, innovators, and exemplary Americans will have their stars dampened, condemned to a life of uncertainty -- fearing that any moment their lives could be uprooted, deported to countries they know nothing about.
We all know that the Supreme Court is a rabid dog that can and will ruin everything that we as Americans hold dear, but when do we stand up and do something about it? Well, the time where we actually can do something about it is far sooner than the 2065 date experts project.
The moment that we reclaim power in DC, Democrats can and must alter the makeup of the Supreme Court by packing it with liberal justices.

# **Iran seizes control of Strait of Hormuz, threatening fragile peace deal after days of reignited violence**
Iran declared Sunday that **[all vessels must obtain permission from the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps](https://substack.com/redirect/8e85e31c-d464-4086-bced-3544c643282a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** before navigating the Strait of Hormuz, asserting sole management of the waterway for the next 30 days. The announcement follows Iranian drone strikes on two commercial ships -- a Singapore-flagged cargo vessel and a Panama-flagged tanker -- prompting US retaliatory airstrikes on Iranian targets and Iranian missile and drone attacks against US allies Bahrain and Kuwait.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8e85e31c-d464-4086-bced-3544c643282a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

* **The escalation has effectively collapsed shipping traffic through the strait,** dropping from 40-50 ships daily earlier in the week to just 10 on Saturday -- approaching pre-peace deal levels. Experts warn vessels remain too fearful to transit freely, compared to more than 130 ships crossing daily before the war began.

Fellow American,

**_In Special Forces, when a team calls for backup, you answer. That's exactly why I'm writing to you today._**

I've spent my life serving on the front lines.

First, at West Point.

Then, as a Green Beret in Army Special Forces.

And now in Congress, fighting to secure our border, strengthen our military, and put America First.

The battlefield may look different today, but the mission hasn't changed.

| [ ](http://links.harriganfornc.com/u/click?_t=687026f8d8f7415aa539c5385c376b1f&_m=97d0ee5e7af94ad19f57ce340e6a4987&_e=vF7hOgR6vV7TOI_46oBGTf1MBaPWtszbGOGPdW5ZWZuqwLy2jmfnstB-injIerPsS-DGcpHpNco2ZC8oPN9Xz9CsuKl4cd_QQ9vvnP7qNiSwCnKok4SJll5KoZatlaFT6sG-7Q3D6pOptIAjsVzKZlIlGv4nBbixTrggxFkzsDGtYodINZV9ud_1o9zDfwfHTUxrXmLqgXyCIZUzi3zsT_tzP3aZ026KB6PS-MF8RT_dmKJHAWXhA_J38z40en6IaGJkFpt4_FMpXzn4dWEGyKNq1v6nLsHkiRwDLoBjVWkoyTeoGN0D-Tt91Kj_JG5sVtuMjNMdBIpylkMH8H5XV8w_re7eIWjj7yo0XAVGJIwoV8qgCKV6yL8O9r2SzhDGnZld2NPryq1SX7K7APEqe2B8esf_E-xPsicpQ5IL9rve2s_kLVFSgUHZbg4CatuRASxQfPNfLz03ciZAqTTpH1dTXhlMXdULTUWeoUMKRWJvqQUlA26IluUfDUIu4Ht7zxmrjYnLBgxyBU7lvFHJUfN2eS_67Owzr2qnBMGZ0AI%3D)

name: Wes Moore
subject: Whether we’re beatable
body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1561%2E1086043%2E5jD0Re)
Peter, I’ll be direct:
**We have 3 days left in the most important fundraising quarter of this race yet.** Our next deadline is June 30 and whatever we raise before then tells the country one thing – whether this campaign is strong, or whether it's beatable.
Most people assume Maryland is a safe blue state. **It isn't.**
Two of the last four governors before me were Republicans -- just four years ago, we had one. Re-election is not guaranteed. Now that we have a Republican opponent in Dan Cox, all eyes are on what we’re able to accomplish before this deadline.
**[Can I count on you to chip in any amount before our June 30th deadline?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260628-1.3-t_lE&refcode=em-20260628-1&t=2&akid=1561%2E1086043%2E5jD0Re)**
Peter, if we lose, it sends a signal to every MAGA Republican in the country: a governor with a real record of results can still be knocked out.
I won't let that happen. But a strong June 30 number doesn't come from me. It comes from folks like you. We have to show that enough people believe in our mission to leave no one behind.
**[So I’m asking again: Can you chip in $5 before our deadline to help us finish this quarter strong?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260628-1.3-t_lE&refcode=em-20260628-1&t=3&akid=1561%2E1086043%2E5jD0Re)**

I’m grateful for your support, Peter.
Elevate,
Wes

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. Can I tell you what drives my work in the Senate every day, friend?
I grew up as the proud daughter of a World War II veteran. _That's why_ I'm fighting so hard in the Senate to protect our veterans from Trump's federal funding cuts – all to ensure they get the hard-earned benefits they deserve.
I worked as a cocktail waitress at Caesars Palace to help pay for college, becoming the first in my family to graduate. _That's why_ I'm fighting to improve Nevada’s public schools and increase opportunities for our young people – even as Trump dismantles the Department of Education.

**I grew up in the back of a bar.**
Not a fancy restaurant. Not a supper club. A beer joint, pool hall, and liquor store on Main Street in Central, South Carolina - the Sanitary Cafe. My parents ran it. We lived behind it. I've stood next to kids from small towns just like Central who signed up because they believe in something bigger than themselves.

clean_body: I was the first in my family to go to college. | Peter - Let me tell you something they don't teach you in Washington. I grew up in the back of a bar. Not a fancy restaurant. Not a supper club. A beer joint, pool hall, and liquor store on Main Street in Central, South Carolina - the Sanitary Cafe. My parents ran it. We lived behind it. I swept the floors, wiped down the tables, and fell asleep listening to the sounds of working people winding down after a long shift at the textile mill. Neither of my parents finished high school. But they worked as if the sun were always going down, and they believed - truly believed - that their kids would go further than they did. I was the first in my family to go to college. And while I was there, I lost them both. Mom and Dad, died within two years of each other. I came home on weekends to keep the business going and helped raise my little sister, Darline, who was just 13. I didn't have a safety net. I had no choice but to climb. That's the South Carolina way. That's the American way. After law school, I put on the uniform. I became a U.S. Air Force Judge Advocate - military prosecutor, defense attorney. Even after South Carolinians sent me to the Senate, I kept serving in the Reserves. I've been to Afghanistan. I've been to Iraq. I've stood next to kids from small towns just like Central who signed up because they believe in something bigger than themselves. That's why I fight so hard, because I know exactly what's at stake. The people coming to our family's pool hall after a long week - they weren't asking for much. Safe streets. A fair shot. A chance to build something. Those are the same things Americans want today. And the folks on the other side of the aisle? They're perfectly happy to hand your neighborhood over to open borders, pile new taxes on your paycheck, and tell you to be grateful for it. I won't stand for it. Not for a second. We are in a fight for the future of this country, and it is not a time to sit on the sidelines. I didn't come from money. I came from a bar in South Carolina, a mother who worked hard, and a faith that hard work still means something in America. It still does. Thank you for standing with me. God bless you, and God bless South Carolina. Can I count on you?**](https://sue4ri.com/l/ccXfSHH9N2L3) **This isn’t our first public filing, but it is the last one that makes a material difference before the primary** – _can you believe the primary is less than 3 months away_ 🤯? body:
An independent judge rejected Trump’s politically motivated investigation into me.
#
Peter,
A federal judge rejected the U.S. Department of Justice’s politically motivated investigation into me.
[](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260628-2.yfEhG3&amount=5&refcode=em20260628-806&t=2&akid=806%2E34582%2EBpeFop)
Let me be clear about what happened here: **Donald Trump tried to use the DOJ as his personal revenge factory.**
He ordered a criminal investigation into a political opponent. It was unconstitutional. It was meritless. And a federal judge saw it for exactly what it was.
This is not how America is supposed to work. The Department of Justice does not belong to Donald Trump. It does not exist to intimidate his opponents, punish people who stand up to him, or scare Democrats into silence.
But that is exactly what Trump wants. He wants us looking over our shoulders. He wants us afraid to fight back. He wants anyone who challenges him to wonder if they will be next.
**Let me be clear: I won’t be intimidated. And I don’t think you will be either.**
**[So today, I’m asking you to stand with me. Will you make a contribution of $5 now to show Trump, his allies, and every MAGA politician trying to weaponize power against their opponents that we will not back down?](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260628-2.yfEhG3&amount=5&refcode=em20260628-806&t=3&akid=806%2E34582%2EBpeFop)**

Thank you for having my back.
– Tim Walz

Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville's time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year's Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul "Bear" Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

_In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. In his first term as Senator, Tommy was one of eight Republicans to vote against certifying the 2020 election, has been a strong pro-life advocate, and called out Democrats for being pro-crime.

Now, Coach Tuberville is running for Governor so he can continue representing Alabamians and Americans in his homestate of Alabama. The Radical Left thinks they can flip Alabama blue and turn it into the California of the South. Can he count on your support? _

What your support has helped build (in their words, not ours)
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260628-2972)
Peter,
It’s the last Sustainer Sunday of the quarter, so let’s take a second to look at what you’ve built.
When we launched this campaign, the political class knew exactly how they wanted to talk about Fran.
A foul-mouthed chef and single mom with credit card debt. A democratic socialist from Madison with no billionaire backers, no corporate PAC money, and no support from the establishment.
They expected us to be a non-factor. They said we couldn’t break through.
But then, people started taking notice.
* **Rep. Ro Khanna, U.S. Representative for California’s 17th District** , called Fran “exactly the kind of bold, grassroots-powered leader we need.”
* **Rep. Ilhan Omar, U.S. Representative for Minnesota’s 5th District** , said Fran leads with “moral clarity, compassion, and unmatched courage.”
* **Nina Turner, former Ohio State Senator and national co-chair of Bernie Sanders’ presidential campaign** , is backing Fran because she's “not another cautious, politics-as-usual Democrat waiting for permission to lead.”
* **Qasim Rashid, human rights attorney and progressive advocate** , called Fran “the fighter Wisconsin — and America — needs.”
* **Our Revolution, one of the largest progressive grassroots organizations in the country** , said this “a grassroots movement powered by people — not corporate PACs.”
* **Our Wisconsin Revolution** called Fran “the type of leader Wisconsin not only needs, but deserves.”

**And increasingly, the press is seeing what this movement has been building.**
* Back in February, [John Nichols wrote in _The Capital Times_ wrote](https://act.francescahong.com/go/14771?t=1&akid=2972%2E105371%2Evy-cet) that Fran’s campaign is getting noticed “in Wisconsin and nationally.”
* [Dan Shafer at _The Recombobulation Area_ wrote](https://act.francescahong.com/go/13323?t=2&akid=2972%2E105371%2Evy-cet) that “Hong currently has momentum,” calling Fran “the candidate everyone seemed to be talking about.”
* [NBC News reported this week](https://act.francescahong.com/go/14772?t=3&akid=2972%2E105371%2Evy-cet) that Fran has seen “a surge of momentum” in a crowded Democratic primary.

**And on the question of “electability”? Folks are answering that, too.**
Because all across the country, voters are proving that candidates who fight unapologetically for working people are not liabilities. They are exactly what this moment demands.

name: Justin Kwasa, LCV
subject: TAKE ACTION: Tell USPS – Hands Off Our Votes!
body:
To view this mail in a browser, copy https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTM4MDg3MDkS1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjQ4MDkyMDc2NAS2&mt=1&rt=0 into your browser.
Tell the U.S. Postal Service: Hands Off Our Votes!

The Trump administration is trying, yet again, to interfere with free and fair
elections and keep people from voting. This latest anti-voter power grab is
through the United States Postal Service, which has proposed new rules that
could prevent millions of eligible Americans from voting by mail.

USPS’s job is to deliver mail, not decide who gets a ballot. This proposed rule
would disenfranchise large numbers of voters, including immigrant voters, rural
voters, voters of color, Tribal voters, and voters with disabilities. We won’t
stand for it.

Public comments are open until July 2nd and USPS and Trump need to hear us loud
and clear: Hands Off Our Votes!

Tell the U.S. Postal Service: Hands Off Our Votes! https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/~ ADD YOUR NAME https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/rNykfE~P6phG/M2lsaFM0aUdYSGtRQ0x0U2dwN0ptdlZ2YUJoNGtGSG0rTEhaZ0xObC9KNWE1NW5NZkJvTjY0UzNydmU2Q25DdGVLTWVEUXJiSncrQXFOOFc3cmtwNjFPbUxpSGdBNVp6SlB0VjdpcjNHUHc9S0/UHkxT1JESC9FZTlMSFR5aHYxbkliUnlJS1BRWlQzTkdXdW9rVURtRjZ3N3ZaWjdxRVByQkR1Q0FIVVNVdE1HVFJwTkUvUVRBbHhVQWJocUpzVWxwOVlIdUpkTmRvcnk5Q2ZXNXI0dGdjT2M9S0 Peter, The Trump administration is trying, yet again, to interfere with free and fair
elections and keep people from voting. This latest anti-voter power grab is
through the United States Postal Service (USPS), which has proposed new rules
that could prevent millions of eligible Americans from voting by mail. Add your name today and tell the U.S. Postal Service: Hands Off Our Votes! >> https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/G8bxcK2V~LJ~/M2lsaFM0aUdYSGtRQ0x0U2dwN0ptdlZ2YUJoNGtGSG0rTEhaZ0xObC9KNWE1NW5NZkJvTjY0UzNydmU2Q25DdGVLTWVEUXJiSncrQXFOOFc3cmtwNjFPbUxpSGdBNVp6SlB0VjdpcjNHUHc9S0/UHkxT1JESC9FZTlMSFR5aHYxbkliUnlJS1BRWlQzTkdXdW9rVURtRjZ3N3ZaWjdxRVByQkR1Q0FIVVNVdE1HVFJwTkUvUVRBbHhVQWJocUpzVWxwOVlIdUpkTmRvcnk5Q2ZXNXI0dGdjT2M9S0 The Postal Service's job is to deliver mail, not decide who gets a ballot. The
new rule would essentially put USPS in the position of deciding who can vote by
mail, which is not its job, not what postal workers are trained to do, and a
violation of the Constitution. It would require the federal government to keep a
list of voters they think should be allowed to vote and then use USPS to track when and how those votes
are cast. These actions would create real barriers to voter participation in
elections, and have no place in a healthy democracy. Voting by mail is essential for millions of people — it’s proven safe, secure,
and trusted by election administrators across the country. This proposed rule is
designed to disenfranchise large numbers of voters, including immigrant voters,
rural voters, voters of color, Tribal voters, and voters with disabilities. And
the kicker is, Trump himself voted by mail earlier this year! In 2024, nearly one-third of voters — tens of millions of people — voted by
mail. These proposed changes would make it harder or impossible for many of us
to vote in the accessible and safe ways that we require. USPS must abandon this
proposal and instead focus on its core mission of providing reliable,
affordable, universal mail service — especially for all voting and
election-related mail. This Rule is unconstitutional, impractical, and impossible to implement without
silencing voters in the 2026 general election. We must all take action today and
urge the U.S. Postal Service to defend the independence of our election systems,
as well as their own independence. The more comments that are submitted, the clearer our message: Hands Off Our
Votes! Throughout history, omens like comets and meteors have been read either as forebearers of good luck and coming change, or of approaching catastrophe. At this moment in American history, we stand at a crossroads and could head either way.
Nowhere is this more apparent than in Louisiana where MAGA has used their complete control of state power to declare a 'state of emergency, launching a full tilt fascist assault unparalleled to anywhere else in the nation.
They've implemented a slate of the most extreme far-right policies in modern US history, they deployed the national guard to New Orleans, rushed through Jim Crow style maps, cancelled our elections, and conducted a coup to eliminate a sitting Democratic US Congressman. We all fear what comes next.

Peter,

Before that happens, I’m hoping there’s something I can say to convince you to make your first donation to help us hit our $1.5 million goal.

body:
I acknowledge there's a very good chance you didn't wake up and think "I am going to make a contribution to Elissa Slotkin today. I get it.

| | | | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
Hello. It's Elissa Slotkin.

I acknowledge there's a very good chance you didn't wake up this morning and think "I am going to make a contribution to Elissa Slotkin today." I get it.

But that is what I am asking you to do.

I am one of a small number of Democratic Senators who won their race at the same time Donald Trump won that state.

Over the next few months, I am going to travel a bit and help Democrats in tough races -- like I've done for a number of candidates and in a number of "red" states already. But we're just getting started.

Here in Michigan, we also have an open Senate seat, a governor's race and a number of other close races. I know how to find voters in so-called "red' areas and can help make the difference -- something that will be important after some tough primaries.

[**If making sure Democrats have a chance of retaking the Senate, the House and supporting candidates in tough races is important to you, I am asking you to make a contribution before our FEC fundraising deadline ends to help make that happen.**](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/3865?refcode=em260628&t=1&akid=2476%2E135344%2Ec8cxde)

name: Chris Pappas
subject: A literal gold mine in Azerbaijan
body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1001&akid=7454%2E582294%2EjCPLYI ]Chris Pappas for Senate[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1002&akid=7454%2E582294%2EjCPLYI ]Chris Pappas for Senate

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260628_3.IyCw4C&refcode=em20260628-7454&amount=5&t=1003&akid=7454%2E582294%2EjCPLYI ][IMG]
Josh Rogers/NHPR

In this week’s GOP debate, John Sununu told a roomful of Republicans he's
running for Senate to send me back to "bussing tables” at my family’s
“chicken restaurant."

He meant it as an insult. As if the people who work in restaurants — who
cook your food, clear your plates, keep family businesses that are the
heart of our state alive — have something to be embarrassed about.

I’m not embarrassed. I’m proud.

My family opened our restaurant over 100 years ago. I know what a 65-hour
week feels like because I've worked one. I know what it means to show up
every day, work hard, and treat the people around you like they matter —
because they do.

John Sununu has never had to work hard a day in his life. He was born into
the Sununu political dynasty. His family's "business" isn't a restaurant
serving New Hampshire families. It owns a literal gold mine in Azerbaijan
that sells minerals to China.

That's what John Sununu calls “honest work.”

New Hampshire workers deserve a senator who knows what a hard day's labor
actually looks like — who fights for small business owners, for restaurant
workers, for every family just trying to make ends meet. John Sununu is
running to protect people like himself. I'm running for everyone else.

He showed us who he is with these elitist comments. Now let’s make sure he
doesn’t represent us.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260628_3.IyCw4C&amount=5&refcode=em20260628-3&t=1022&akid=7454%2E582294%2EjCPLYI ]Donate $5 »

John Sununu doesn’t know the real New Hampshire. He doesn’t get how hard
we work — and he sure as hell doesn’t think our labor is worth respecting.

I do. That’s why I’m running for Senate.

— Chris Pappas

My job is to make sure we're not only raising enough money to elect Alex in this race, but to help make sure the donations we receive are spent in the most cost-effective way.
We are staring at our official FEC fundraising deadline in less than 72 hours, and we are still short of our goal to file a great report and keep us on pace to win. I’m feeling a little queasy, but there’s still time to turn our fortunes around.
Now, I am sure you didn't wake up this morning, jump out of bed, and scream, "Today is the day I am going to donate to Alex Vindman for Senate!" but I really hope you will.
$3. That is the request from Alex.
$3 to win this race.

We just WON our runoff election in Louisiana by a landslide!
This is Jamie Davis, the lifelong family farmer and now the Democrat Nominee running to flip Louisiana’s OPEN US Senate.
We are on the cusp of making history: a Black person has never represented the entire state of Louisiana in the US Senate. But this is our moment. The Miracle on the Mississippi is alive and well.
[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
We didn’t do this with billionaires or untraceable PAC donors. We did this solely with the contributions of individuals across the country—over 54,600 donors currently—who believe in what we can do when we stand up for the people and fight for the needs of working people.
I never thought I would be standing here as the Democratic nominee for US Senate in my beloved Louisiana. I farm the same land my grandfather worked as a sharecropper and we just sent a resounding message that we are not going back.
When I am elected, I will be the first Black US Senator to be elected in Louisiana since Reconstruction.
James Carville was so inspired by our performance that he said Democrats now have a “fighting chance” to flip Louisiana’s open US Senate seat blue. He’s right—but now we have to fight for it together.
It is no exaggeration to say that we just became MAGA’s top target in November. We are going to need everybody joining with us to compete against MAGA billionaires and oligarchs who want to buy this state. Will you donate $25, $50 or whatever you can to fuel the Miracle on the Mississippi? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
HELP ME FLIP THIS SENATE SEAT! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
Thank you, thank you, thank you for everything. This is a fight for the soul of this country, and Louisiana is leading the way.
I am so proud to be leading us in this moment. And I will not let you down.
Sincerely,

Both parties have a problem. Too many politicians, Democrat and Republican alike, spend more time chasing cable news hits than solving the real problems their constituents face every day. They listen to lobbyists, follow party bosses, and wonder why trust in government keeps falling.
**I 'm tired of it** (and you can join us **here** if you are too)**.**
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/e7c6dbeb-9b5e-4287-ae3c-9b21cf86cb6f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**" Hometowns Over Headlines" is different.** It isn't some "Make America __ Again" lie, it's a governing philosophy. It means showing up in Sequatchie County on a Saturday morning when no cameras are rolling. It means sitting down with WSMV to talk about a bill on algorithmic pricing that affects what your family pays at the grocery store. It means marching in Rutherford Pride and shaking hands with 82nd Airborne veterans in the same weekend, because **every** community deserves to be seen.
**[Chip in today, because hometowns win when neighbors show up for each other. Today is the last day to hit our goal for the week! Let 's win this!](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/753e9fd6-a7ce-4d11-967f-7121b22dc203?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[DONATE $15 HERE!](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/753e9fd6-a7ce-4d11-967f-7121b22dc203?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Washington rewards the loud and the flashy. Our team is building something different as a campaign rooted in the belief that neighbors, teachers, small business owners, and working families are worth more than the headlines they never make.
The primary is August 6th. **We are already halfway through the year and need the manpower to keep it up these next two months.** We are building this race one conversation and one contribution at a time. This campaign doesn't run on PAC money, it runs on people like you who believe Tennessee deserves better. _[Can I count on you today?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/753e9fd6-a7ce-4d11-967f-7121b22dc203?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_

Too many politicians, Democrat and Republican alike, spend more time chasing cable news hits than solving the real problems their constituents face every day. They listen to lobbyists, follow party bosses, and wonder why trust in government keeps falling. I 'm tired of it (and you can join us here if you are too). | | ---|---|--- " Hometowns Over Headlines" is different. It isn't some "Make America Again" lie, it's a governing philosophy. It means showing up in Sequatchie County on a Saturday morning when no cameras are rolling. It means sitting down with WSMV to talk about a bill on algorithmic pricing that affects what your family pays at the grocery store. It means marching in Rutherford Pride and shaking hands with 82nd Airborne veterans in the same weekend, because every community deserves to be seen. Washington rewards the loud and the flashy. Our team is building something different as a campaign rooted in the belief that neighbors, teachers, small business owners, and working families are worth more than the headlines they never make. The primary is August 6th. We are already halfway through the year and need the manpower to keep it up these next two months. We are building this race one conversation and one contribution at a time. This campaign doesn't run on PAC money, it runs on people like you who believe Tennessee deserves better. body:
# [](https://act.electjon.com/go/4629?t=1&akid=2431%2E5691347%2E2xCuno)

Hi Peter —
[**I’m writing to ask, humbly, if you will chip in $5 to my reelection campaign ahead of our important FEC fundraising deadline this Tuesday.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-jun26.Bh0QdH&refcode=em260628-2-f&utm_campaign=em260628-2-f&t=2&akid=2431%2E5691347%2E2xCuno)
Here’s why this request is so important, especially today:
The end of this month marks the most important fundraising deadline we’ve faced so far in our campaign, and one of the most critical tests of the movement we’ve built in Georgia.
After the deadline, we’re legally required to report our fundraising numbers to the Federal Election Commission — and shortly after, those numbers will be made public.
Everyone from Donald Trump to my Republican opponent and their billionaire allies are going to look at our fundraising numbers closely. Very closely.
If they think we look weak, you can bet they’ll flood the airwaves with even more attack ads designed to distort my record.
We have to show everyone that our movement in Georgia is thriving and unstoppable — that we have what it takes to build the strongest voter outreach and mobilization program our state has ever seen. Because that’s what it’s going to take to win this race.
That’s why I’m personally asking:

Peter,
We have 5 days until the June 30 FEC deadline that closes out our second quarter - and one of our best supporters who believes in this campaign just made it more interesting. They gave $6,000 and challenged the rest of us to rise to meet it.

They'll certainly outspend us on fancy television ads. But they can't outwork us at the doors and they'll never exceed the over 1500 individuals like you who have supported our campaign.
We don't need the most money, but we can only win if we have the resources to tell our story, and the people and the gas money to send organizers into every one of our 26 counties.
One neighbor put $6,000 on the line for the ground game. Let's show them they're not alone. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/clark-eoq?refcode=62826_EOQ_2]

body:
Will you fill out my Issues Survey before 8 AM tomorrow?
These emails are the best way for our campaign to stay in touch with supporters like you. If you'd prefer to unsubscribe, [click here](https://act.mandelabarnes.com/go/7010?refcode=LOC_EM_SURV_2026.06.28_Issues-Survey_B2_F1_S1_C1_actives-exp_RS-T0&t=1&akid=6408%2E196590%2E1CVuv4).

| [](https://act.mandelabarnes.com/go/7382?refcode=LOC_EM_SURV_2026.06.28_Issues-Survey_B2_F1_S1_C1_actives-exp_RS-T0&t=4&akid=6408%2E196590%2E1CVuv4) Do you have a minute? It’s Mandela Barnes.

When you’re building a grassroots movement like ours, you can’t just talk; you have to listen. I’ve visited all 72 counties in Wisconsin because I know the way we’ll win this race is by fighting for the issues that matter most to working-class families – from Bayfield to Kenosha.

But I don’t always get a chance to connect with folks in person. So we’ll have to settle for the next best option: [**_Will you fill out my Issues Survey to let me know what’s most important to you right now? I need your response before my 8:00 AM meeting with my campaign team tomorrow._**](https://act.mandelabarnes.com/go/7382?refcode=LOC_EM_SURV_2026.06.28_Issues-Survey_B2_F1_S1_C1_actives-exp_RS-T0&t=5&akid=6408%2E196590%2E1CVuv4) | | [ TAKE MY ISSUES SURVEY -> ](https://act.mandelabarnes.com/go/7382?refcode=LOC_EM_SURV_2026.06.28_Issues-Survey_B2_F1_S1_C1_actives-exp_RS-T0&t=6&akid=6408%2E196590%2E1CVuv4)
---
**This race for Wisconsin Governor is a pure TOSS-UP.**

If Donald Trump and his MAGA billionaires flip this seat red, we’ll be dealing with an agenda that puts voting rights at risk, drives up costs, and cuts access to healthcare.

That’s exactly why your voice matters right now. What drives our campaign is the issues that matter most to everyday people like you.

[**_So, pelase, will you take 2 minutes to fill out my Issues Survey and tell me what’s most important to you? We got thousands of responses from our last survey, and we don’t want you to miss out on this opportunity to make your voice heard!_**](https://act.mandelabarnes.com/go/7382?refcode=LOC_EM_SURV_2026.06.28_Issues-Survey_B2_F1_S1_C1_actives-exp_RS-T0&t=7&akid=6408%2E196590%2E1CVuv4)

I’ll be watching the responses as they come in.

– Mandela
